name: Ian Calderon
subject: An important update on our campaign
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ian Calderon for Governor 2026
body:
My campaign ends today, but my commitment to California does not.

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/NQQPgDyiei8BXre3JuGcyw~~/AAUS1hA~/xKqIqJPZXjvw-g0KWdHpaq6rrAmQucP9ULN0FKbWNIResl_mkG-8Qlxl-WNFIvf4GfEszLEceCFtAdXpQ9WIzno4b6aORsMO9nLhs9lpXYt0CCvIuxKnw_PUJ3JlyYAT)
| | Dear Friends, I have always believed that my message about affordability, accountability, and the need for a new generation of leadership would resonate with voters. But in a race of this scale, a message only matters if you have the resources to ensure Californians can actually see and hear it. After thoughtful consideration, I have decided to support Congressman Eric Swalwell because the challenges facing California are bigger than any one campaign. California needs leadership that is ready to govern on day one, and I believe Eric can carry forward many of the priorities our campaign worked hard to elevate. On the campaign trail, I saw firsthand the challenges Californians face every day. Too many families struggle to access basic necessities like nearby health care, and too many communities lack clean drinking water. Californians are ready for real change, and restoring trust in government requires more than words — it requires concrete solutions that make life better today and build a foundation for tomorrow. As a former Assembly Majority Leader, I know progress only happens when leaders bring people together and build strong partnerships. Eric has the experience, energy, and determination to lead California — and he has what it takes to win. **Will you stand with me and**[**donate**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/d5duMJ7zSt3NDYQF0oJcWA~~/AAUS1hA~/RLzWEk7ugn0t1aoQIdOLRpBS2T_LVBiWqu_70kGVQ6MIVGKoMWu8ES63QToBuJCNneg5qk5bwiPBbTGeVh9eiBWvF8RdUxajNadEyldypE8mhxN4bZXzMvCL_NaN8mJxBFeukWy4kENBZZNOpnz35RfmFwQOV9UoN1EmqIuK03g~)**to Eric’s campaign today?** Finally, I want to thank you — from the bottom of my heart — for your support, encouragement, and belief in our work. Campaigns are powered by people like you, and I am grateful for every conversation and every contribution. While my campaign ends today, my commitment to California and the people who call it home does not. Let’s continue to build a California where families can afford to live, communities are safe, and people can trust their government to deliver. Yours, Ian

name: Mai Vang
subject: The daughter of refugees
body:
I wanted to share a little more about who I am and why I’m running for Congress.

| | | | | | [|
---](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=ffd3464410&e=dd5af5b7b1)
| | | | | | Hi friends,

---
| | [**I wanted to share a little more about who I am and why I’m running for Congress. I hope you’ll read this message, and if it speaks to you, chip in $5 or whatever you can to help us build a winning campaign in CA-07.**](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=3dc7a1d7a6&e=dd5af5b7b1)
I’m the daughter of Hmong refugees.

My parents fled the CIA’s secret war in Laos and came to California with just the hope that their children might have opportunities they never had.
---
[|
---](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=dd1424f4f2&e=dd5af5b7b1)
| | I grew up in South Sacramento as the oldest of 16 kids, so responsibility wasn’t something I learned later in life. It was every day.
I helped raise my siblings.I translated for my parents.I showed up when my community needed me.
And those lessons stuck.
When schools in my neighborhood were threatened with closure, I helped organize parents and co-founded _Hmong Innovating Politics_ so families like mine would have a voice.
When immigrant families were being terrorized during the first Trump administration, as a Sacramento School Board member, I championed California’s first Safe Haven Resolution to make sure our schools remained places of safety.
When something isn’t right, I don’t sit quietly and hope it changes. I step up. That’s why I’m running for Congress.
**Families across CA-07 are being squeezed by the cost of living, while our tax dollars get spent on endless wars. Too often Washington listens to corporate PACs like defense contractors instead of the communities we serve. I’m running to change that -- and that’s why I’ve made a commitment not to take corporate PAC money or any money from AIPAC.**
This campaign will only succeed if it’s powered by people.

| | ** FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE ** ** March 5th, 2026** **Contact: Steve Walsh** **702-625-2322‬** **Steve@rmcstrategy.com ** **AMERICA’S TOUGHEST SHERIFF JOE ARPAIO ENDORSES ****LT. COL. DAVID FLIPPO FOR CONGRESS IN NEVADA’S 2ND DISTRICT** RENO, NV — Sheriff Joe Arpaio, America’s Toughest Sheriff and the most iconic figure in law enforcement and border security, today proudly announced his full endorsement of Lt. Col. David Flippo (Ret.) in his campaign for the United States House of Representatives in Nevada’s 2nd Congressional District.
---
|
---
| Sheriff Joe Arpaio was the FIRST major leader in the country to endorse President Trump in 2015.
President Trump has called Sheriff Joe Arpaio “ _An outstanding American patriot,_ ” and once said of Sheriff Arpaio: “ _When Sheriff Joe gives you an endorsement, you know you’re the king of the border._ ”
“ _I am deeply honored to receive the endorsement of Sheriff Joe Arpaio,_ ” said Flippo. “ _Sheriff Joe is a true American hero. He kept our country safe and stepped up for President Trump. Sheriff Joe led the way for America for decades, and I couldn’t be more honored to have him on our team._”
Sheriff Arpaio will be holding events with David Flippo in NV-2 later this month, and details will be announced soon.
Flippo is running to deliver servant-leadership, integrity, and an uncompromising America First agenda to Congress. He has earned enthusiastic endorsements from prominent conservatives and grassroots champions, including Congressman Paul Gosar, Moms for America Action, Nevada Young Republicans, and Turning Point Action USA.
For more information, visit[ https://www.flippo4nv.com/](https://electdavidflippo.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9aba26b775663b53df718fc1a&id=65cb6669b9&e=273c9a71fb) ###
About David
David Flippo is a battle-tested American patriot and strong leader with a proven record of problem-solving. As a retired Air Force combat commander, he led over 1,000 Airmen and established multiple operating bases during combat operations in Iraq. His military leadership extended to commanding maintenance squadrons responsible for dozens of combat aircraft in Alaska. After retiring, David applied his skills to the private sector, managing maintenance programs for BP’s Alaska oilfields, and now owns two small businesses in Nevada, where he understands firsthand the challenges of inflation, supply chain issues, and rising costs.
Nevada needs leaders like David who put people first by tackling surging crime, failing schools, burdensome regulations, and attacks on Constitutional freedoms. His experience in leadership and fiscal responsibility equips him to rein in government overreach and champion a servant leadership approach for all Nevadans. David Flippo is ready to fight for Nevada with courage and commitment. For more information, visit [flippo4nv.com](https://electdavidflippo.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9aba26b775663b53df718fc1a&id=41c4f70d9a&e=273c9a71fb)

name: David Hogg
subject: This was a warning
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Nida Allam came within 1% of taking down incumbent Rep. Valerie Foushee — that’s the power of our movement.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260305-1&t=1&akid=3219%2E587540%2EzvVJ26)
Peter,
**Nida Allam came within 1% of taking down incumbent Rep. Valerie Foushee.**
Let that sink in.
In the last week alone, over $2 million in special interest money flooded the race to defeat her — **and she was still only 1,200 votes from victory.**
Margins this razor-thin tell us something important: **Voters are paying attention, and they’re done settling for politics as usual.** They want bold progressives who will fight relentlessly for working families, who won’t bow to corporate greed, and who refuse to back down, even when the odds are stacked against them.
This wasn’t just a close race, it was a warning. It’s proof that when young, forward-thinking progressives step up to challenge the status quo, they don’t just make noise, they shake up the entire system.
Asleep-at-the-wheel incumbents who think they can coast through another cycle on corporate cash and name recognition should consider themselves put on notice. **Fearless fighters like Nida who will meet this moment with courage and moral clarity are the future of the Democratic Party.**
And we did exactly what Leaders We Deserve was built to do — challenge complacent incumbents and force them to fight for their seat, make this race contentious, and show that people-power _can_ move the needle, even against massive dark money spending.
We aren’t going to stop fighting, Peter. Every progressive candidate that runs and every dollar we raise is another chance to continue building the movement we need to win real solutions for working families and reshape the Democratic Party.
Thank you for your support in helping us make our party better. Challenges like this are never easy but few things worth doing ever are and your support makes our work possible.
**[If you’re with us, can you pitch in $5 today to help Leaders We Deserve keep taking on the establishment and backing bold progressive leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260305_1_nida.goHygs&refcode=em20260305-3219&amount=5&t=2&akid=3219%2E587540%2EzvVJ26)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

body:
Donald Trump came to Georgia.

The White House sent him here to do damage control on tariffs and health care.

But he just couldn’t help himself: instead of trying to defend his price-inflating tariffs and insurance-premium-doubling health care policy, he resorted to repeating conspiracy theories about the 2020 election — an election he lost in Georgia despite pressuring Georgia election officials to “find” him more votes.

Maybe he’s been watching the rallies I’ve been holding across Georgia, where thousands have turned out in opposition to his corruption and depravity. Because he took a moment to throw some insults my way.

Now, Donald Trump has been insulting me for a long time. But this time, it didn’t seem like his heart was in it. I think you could see in his eyes and hear in his voice that he knows he’s lost the American people. That he knows his Presidency is slipping away. That he can feel Georgians, and people nationwide, preparing to deliver a decisive rebuke of historic abuses of power.

Because as I travel across Georgia, what I hear is more and more people of every background and belief reject Trump’s chaos and corruption. And it's not just Democrats and independents. It’s Republicans too!

More and more Republicans take me aside, or they call me on the phone. They tell me they don’t like where this President has taken us. And they tell me they’re going to support a Democrat for the first time.

But here’s the thing: as he gets more desperate, his abuses become more dangerous. From sending Tulsi Gabbard on ballot raids in Fulton County, Georgia, to threatening a national takeover of elections, we have to be ready for anything.

We have to turn out LANDSLIDE margins of victory ... victories so decisive that no scheme or plot hatched in the White House can foil the will of the people.

And we have to defend voting rights with unprecedented tenacity and resources.

**I need your help to do these things.**

Iran's navy is at the bottom of the ocean. Everyone's covering the missiles. [Nobody's covering the oil](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=484ae7d764&e=567664f14c). 87% of Iran's oil goes to China — and that changes everything about why Trump struck.
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=cd09936dae&e=567664f14c)
| |
🔥 **THE IRAN STORY NOBODY IS COVERING — FOLLOW THE OIL**
87% of Iran's oil goes to China. 55% of Venezuela's does too. Trump isn't just taking out a regime — he's squeezing China's energy supply from two continents at the same time.
The US now produces more oil than Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The Strait of Hormuz matters to China, not us. When you see the numbers side by side, the entire strategy clicks.

🚨 **FIRST TORPEDO SINKING SINCE WWII — IRAN'S NAVY IS GONE**
A US submarine sank an Iranian warship off Sri Lanka with a single torpedo. First time since 1945. The video is unreal.
Missile fire down 86%. Drones down 73%. The US just shifted from long-range strikes to flying directly overhead. Mark breaks down what that transition means — and why the military says they have plenty of munitions to finish this.

🗳️ **TALARICO WINS TEXAS**

body:

**1,000 NEW Housing Units Coming to West Philadelphia** _Construction on the NEW Westpark Apartments has started_ Senator Hughes was thrilled to celebrate the groundbreaking for construction and redevelopment of the Westpark Apartments at 46th and Market Street. The Philadelphia Housing Authority welcomed Senator Hughes, Governor Josh Shapiro, Mayor Cherelle Parker, Westpark residents, and other local community leaders to celebrate the start of the work that will make the Westpark apartments and surrounding space a thriving spot for both residents and local businesses. The project will be completed in phases. Phase 1 will deliver:
* **327 New & Renovated Homes:** 140 of those units will be specifically reserved for returning Westpark residents.
* **Affordability:** Over 150 affordable housing units will be designated for households earning between 20% and 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI).
* **Transit & Connectivity:** A new pedestrian plaza will link the campus directly to the 46th and Market Street SEPTA station.
* **Green Space:** Over an acre of open space, featuring a playground and a public lawn.

* * *
_[Senator Hughes explains](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16703) why the start of construction on this project is such a big deal for West Philadelphia_ [](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16703)
* * *
Continue to follow us on [Facebook](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16704), [Instagram](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16705), [TikTok](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16706), [X](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16707), and [BlueSky](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171480.172709.49&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16708) for the latest news on these new housing units and other affordable housing projects that are being developed in our district.

Dear Peter:

**COURAGE.**

It takes plenty of it to do the hard and uncomfortable work.

Kristi Noem has been a terrible Secretary to the Department of Homeland Security. The worst.

Under her leadership, ICE agents have terrorized our streets and communities. They have detained, deported, brutalized and killed our friends and neighbors. They have arrested children. Has she apologized or worked to admit and correct her mistakes? NO.

Under her leadership, DHS has wasted our money. She has leased a $70 million luxury party jet. She spent $200 million on an advertising campaign - advertising herself. She has been issuing multi-million dollar contracts with little vetting and accountability. Has she stopped this kind of behavior? NO!

Under her leadership, FEMA has failed this country. Red and blue cities are still recovering from disasters with zero money from FEMA. Los Angeles and Altadena are two of those cities. Has she apologized for the delays and pledges to get the money to us? HELL NO!

This lady has been a hot mess.

This week, Kristi Noem found herself before my committee. She brought no answers or remorse. I brought receipts.

I think Kristi thought she was going to be OK. I think Kristi thought we wouldn't ask the hard questions.

Kristi was wrong.

And now she is going to be gone.

Leadership matters and credibility is crucial. Americans need to have faith that those who run our government agencies - people who oversee billions of our taxpayer dollars and are responsible for our safety and freedoms - have good ethics and clear judgement. It does matter.

It is my responsibility to hold them accountable when they do wrong by my constituents.

It takes courage to ask the tough questions that others won't. That happened this week. It had to.

We must keep showing up. From now until November and beyond.

That is how we must fight if we want to win.

**_I want us to win._**

subject: Retired Navy Rear Admiral Condemns Attacks on Her Military Service, Reaffirms Focus on Defeating Lauren Boebert
body:
| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=7645d74642&e=1c5f08419c)
| | | | |
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE****Date:** March 5, 2026 **Contact:**[**Taylor Gillespie**](mailto:taylorg@eileenforcolorado.com)**, 720-557-6185**
**Retired Navy Rear Admiral Condemns Attacks on Her Military Service, Reaffirms Focus on Defeating Lauren Boebert**
**Highlands Ranch, CO -** Retired U.S. Navy Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher, a Democratic candidate for Congress challenging Lauren Boebert, is responding to recent attacks on her 34 years of military service by Trisha Calvarese, including being called a “traitor” and false claims about her service in the United States Navy.Laubacher retired from the Navy in 2024 after nearly four decades in uniform, serving under six presidents from both parties while raising a family through deployments and frequent moves around the world.Her Democratic primary opponent, Trisha Calvarese, has recently attacked Laubacher’s ties to Colorado and falsely suggested that her decades in uniform amounted to working for Donald Trump.Laubacher said the attacks misrepresent the nature of military service and disrespect the sacrifices made by service members and their families.“After 34 years in the United States Navy, serving under six presidents from both parties, I never imagined I would be attacked for wearing the uniform of this country,” said **Retired Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher**. “The day after Veterans Day, my opponent called me a ‘traitor.’ Now she’s trying to claim that my decades of service somehow amounted to working for Donald Trump. That’s simply false and it’s an insult to every service member who swears an oath to the Constitution — not to a president or a political party.”“I know what it’s like to move your family, miss holidays, and serve far from home for decades,” said **Mike Smith, retired Navy Commander, Veterans for Responsible Leadership.** “Eileen Laubacher lived that life honorably. To attack her service as if it were political is not just false — it’s deeply hurtful to every veteran and military family who has made those same sacrifices.”Laubacher said she expected false political attacks on her service when she entered a race against Boebert but did not expect them to be used in a Democratic primary.“When I decided to run against Lauren Boebert, people warned me about the kind of attacks I might face,” Laubacher said. “I expected that from Lauren Boebert and her allies. body:
Now, the GOP is coming after me, full throttle.
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104328?t=6&akid=23196%2E878179%2Edkt5vI) Folks, I said what I said.

**I’d rather stick forks in my eyes than listen to Donald Trump spew his bullshit.**

Now, the GOP is coming after me, full throttle.

They’re calling me “unhinged.” A “lunatic.” They say it’s “gross behavior.” A “DEM MELTDOWN.” I’ve even been diagnosed with “Trump Derangement Syndrome” (let’s pray they find a cure!).

I call it being honest — a foreign concept to the Republican Party, I know.

Trump’s State of the Union address was yet another _dishonest and incoherent rant._ He spent two hours telling lies about America “winning” and shifting blame for his administration’s failures.

He even went as far as to say that Minnesota’s immigrant communities remind us that “there are large parts of the world where corruption and lawlessness are the norm, not the exception.”

Trump: I can tell you what’s really happening in Minnesota and our country. Our communities are traumatized by ICE, life is straight-up unaffordable and folks are _fed up_ with this administration’s recklessness.

America deserves better. Minnesota deserves better.

Peter,
Nothing pisses me off more than getting a fundraising text from Democrats talking about how they’re fighting fascism... Because it’s such B.S. We’re not idiots. Everyone knows most of them aren’t doing jack right now to fight back.
People are being kidnapped into unmarked vans by masked police. There is a genocide happening in Palestine. Literal billionaires have taken over our government. And all Democratic leadership can do is send us another fundraising text?
My name is Graham Platner, and I’m the Marine Corps veteran and Democrat running for U.S. Senate against Susan Collins here in Maine. I’m not going to speak in platitudes or shy away from what I believe. There is a war going on in this country, and the oligarchy and the fascists are winning right now.
Susan Collins is the most vulnerable Republican senator in the country. We have an opportunity to replace her with a working-class Democrat – one who won’t take money from corporations or AIPAC.
But I’m not a wealthy guy, and we’re still short of our $50,000 goal and what we need to win. If I’m going to be able to defeat Susan Collins and flip this Senate seat blue, I need folks like you to chip in now to my campaign.
Please, will you split a donation right now between my campaign and Outrage then Action PAC to help me defeat Susan Collins, flip Maine blue, and take back the Senate with a Democrat who will actually fight to defend our democracy like Democrats oughta be? # We're Endorsing Both Republicans.
This Is the Play.
Take Back California is endorsing Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton — both of them, simultaneously.That's not indecision. That's the strategy.California's top-two primary doesn't care about party affiliation. The two candidates with the most votes advance to November — period. With nine Democrats fracturing their base and the Republican field rapidly consolidating, the window for two Republicans in the general election is opening. Fast.

Chad Bianco is the Riverside County Sheriff who built a grassroots coalition from the ground up. Law enforcement credibility. Real California roots. The kind of candidate who wins votes in places Newsom's team doesn't see coming.Steve Hilton is a national media presence with the name ID and the donor network to compete at scale. He's been making the case against California's failed progressive experiment for years — to a national audience.Together, they cover the field. Together, they lock up enough of the Republican vote to deny Democrats a top-two sweep. And if both make November, California conservatives get a historic choice — and Sacramento gets a wakeup call either way.This hasn't been done in the modern top-two era. We're doing it now.
| IN CALIFORNIA HISTORY, TWO REPUBLICANS HAVE NEVER FACED EACH OTHER IN A GOVERNOR'S GENERAL ELECTION.
WE INTEND TO MAKE HISTORY.

This week my bill to create an emergency egress at Wintergreen Ski Resort passed the House. According to the Fire Chief Curtis Sheets, he has worked with many congressmen on this issue over the last 25 years with no result. Based on that past, he was skeptical it could be done. When the Fire Chief told me about this issue at a site visit back in August, my incredible team got to work and I built bridges needed to get it done in the US Senate and the House. By the grace of God we passed the bill. A highlight for me was bringing the Fire Chief to D.C. to testify on this issue. It really is amazing what we can achieve when we work as a team. # FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
---
|
### What's happening on Friday night?
Candidates and organizations host events throughout the city the night before the Convention. Delegates & Guests enjoy these lively social events! There will also be a chance to pick up your credentials at a pre-registration event hosted at the AC Marriott. Many decide to spend the night on Friday.
View our hotel blocks here: [https://massgop.com/massgop-convention-2026-hotels/](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kzQe8nlkAUU_rzyOJAENZqZ7Y82s-KnTYfRindY9WaryT0gB98iRWTm_Ma6MUpHgPTXMvhaoXRNg1rvSBdHdCx1D74yiRCpqeRLZ9etGptwD05mc7VyhO_04DkvluZNVZyhSYKp3Skh_0Ad2wyqrLovRVxM03khtJSuagtac21lahiffIEvZoCWb78w0NFXUxl7ikOSyaes=&c=FZbe6glPTpxYEjGBZYZoSp8gOQtky8-81QfMtA_dRxywez8T55-R_w==&ch=i8Ey3kwP-drt578afIwWEpRfyA29VNdTHoxL_lC-XY4YnB_ft7D8SQ==)

### How long should I plan to be at the Convention on Saturday?
Convention is a full day affair, plan to be there for a full business day. Right now, that means you should plan to be in the building from 9a-5pm.

### Who will speak from the national scene?
At least one guest speaker has been confirmed, with additional speakers still in the process of being finalized! Past speakers include Congressman Byron Donalds (R-Florida) and Tom Homan.

### Will there be a vendor hall?
Yes. MassGOP State Committeeman Chris Ryan has been appointed as the vendor manager - [Geolopes@comcast.net](mailto:Geolopes@comcast.net).
You can expect Media & Candidate Tables, Private Vendors and Non-Profits to be located inside the Convention building but outside of the arena.

### Will there be food & beverage available?
Yes, the DCU Concession stands will be open and operating.

### Will there be assigned seats?
Town & City Ward Committees have assigned seating areas. Delegates will be directed where to find the location of their committee after check-in.

### What is the dress code?
Dress code is business, but this is a convention, so expect a wide range from suits to American flags head to toe. Have fun with it and dress comfortably!

### Can guests go?
Yes! Guest passes are available at [https://secure.winred.com/massachusetts-gop/2026guestfee](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kzQe8nlkAUU_rzyOJAENZqZ7Y82s-KnTYfRindY9WaryT0gB98iRWQ5_f-u9Z_8rsZTJZR_7to49YB2MttdSO1IEFZ8XBOeWXQvhpwpFYzGQqs0tUZ1KLLruadMnyc8YM37fVIEdsmOrsyHEqb1mWV7OKt-XYzvLcih_b0MeCIK0QLqm4_Y1_87YFa8quBg5BVHocCx4giE=&c=FZbe6glPTpxYEjGBZYZoSp8gOQtky8-81QfMtA_dRxywez8T55-R_w==&ch=i8Ey3kwP-drt578afIwWEpRfyA29VNdTHoxL_lC-XY4YnB_ft7D8SQ==) Guests must pay a fee and do not vote or have access to Committee seating areas.
Who should I contact if I have questions? Your State Committee Members are your best resource for all things Convention.
A list of members is available by district on the MassGOP website here: [https://massgop.com/our-party/committee/](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kzQe8nlkAUU_rzyOJAENZqZ7Y82s-KnTYfRindY9WaryT0gB98iRWbNBkSKxEpf2AoZVPBzxrijKSY4XtdUpQqhshRpdmr88q6irYd30u2QfRH0PU1MCd3lRUw4XgjNRUBXH16969BTrJurLnFNRXA6dsYlAtStgjTrnpXmxf4OpF0GF9HezyQ==&c=FZbe6glPTpxYEjGBZYZoSp8gOQtky8-81QfMtA_dRxywez8T55-R_w==&ch=i8Ey3kwP-drt578afIwWEpRfyA29VNdTHoxL_lC-XY4YnB_ft7D8SQ==)
For questions about delegate report submissions, please contact MassGOP's Political Director Aidan Carey at [aidan@massgop.com](mailto:aidan@massgop.com).

body:
President Trump [fired Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1yqzAUBOCngU6M_oyuCxW3oXPalIxAR-bEEmKkg7HfPkPyCKl3Zme__byNN4cR1_uHS2Ap5HGFo0YggjI-ClbCNUPKO5F7TQXcI-RSR8llz7hivB-9w_gedettAJCgWrDCGGmuF81Nu1gvQE9w0crPwfCez1P4pwWoq56EdzNv0Z5tXPFeCMH5pet9UMJMRvWT0FLIRnPwSLl0XxlXWiDEd35C6eac2mgXoq026n8jh0YOx3F0Ib9OxZk3cthyRMK5NnL4BbFTxPJeCTwLJSe25ATRrZ5VmPeC9GZbrsRcQs8KzLASo72kjLEt1m8Hxoi1N43m9-Qw_gyhP733tPI7AAD__ydnh_Q) on Thursday, making her the first Cabinet secretary to leave in his second term. He named GOP Oklahoma Sen. Markwayne Mullin as her replacement, effective March 31.

## New $6,000 Tax Break for Seniors
As millions of Americans file their [2025 federal tax returns](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-SpCAQxp8GMy1oVMaA4BKzvfRCC6VZ-xZlD9pxfPsr5xU26U5-35_6_nxMH44i7Z-_3YaWQ5p2PEtEZszTV6bCtCfc0sHsXnNG9xVSLhNI6Gupa9lP3lG8prbyNiAC6gqtMgbM0LXSVKtdIPRBq25YJDzmtgsO3dwtalncYIxRFdnbTWrZK6Wk7JreB63MbHQ_qxYUiFaiJ065-Zto5xVDvNITc7OkrYp2Zf4uQv8SMAoYz_NsjuI4eXfdgICxcMqXgHFLO96f3QuLgPGOFTBKfZ_uBnGnlGt2r9qjPxamtNcgoavPNdX_Dhcp0Fv6eAyDUdBKaQSMVbb--6QYqfRGtPJzcxTf7fhHkz4t_A8AAP__mFeIAg), taxpayers 65 and older can claim a brand-new deduction of up to $6,000, or $12,000 for married couples filing jointly. The catch: it requires filing a new [Schedule 1-A](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OozAURp8GOiP_ELwpXGxDl223RAZfw50Y38i-CcPbj5JXmPqTPp1z_t-mm8eEef3nd3Acacpw1ATMUKZ7wcqYCXZ6MvvvuYC_Ryp10lIPQhohhyl4TOfUt8FFAA2mBaes1fZ66aVtN6fABxut9R5U_BPiIr3Rs5ytj8vVyEuL7v0mjRyUUlJeuiFEo-xszTCrXivd9BICMpXuizDzBjGd9ILSLbS3yW3Mj9qYv40eGz0ex9Fhqd1Kr0aPb5lCtDd6XDZY7uKkZxGQcMUZE_IpIhXBG4gMh4C8-bxAEAHCc2Gk_JkrZKRS2-LC48CUsA626eW6e0wfBv5VuJfTPwEAAP__pSOF9A) that many seniors may not know about. This is a thought I've been with. It's not meant to diminish the very real trauma experienced by people, countries, cultures, religions, or communities that have endured war and violence far beyond anything Americans have faced. This is simply an observation about the American experience that I've been thinking about.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/57dc6d2b-950b-4249-a816-3f2ec85eeaa1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
The first Iraq war happened when I was 11 or 12.
9/11 hit when I was 21. I remember exactly where I was. Everybody does.
Then we were told we had to go into Iraq because of weapons of mass destruction. That was the justification. That was the urgency. That was the moral frame.
They never existed.
I protested that war in college. I remember standing there and being told I wasn't patriotic. That I didn't support the troops. That questioning the mission meant questioning America itself. On the other side were people saying no more foreign wars.
That tension? That was democracy. That was freedom of speech. I appreciate that part.
But fast forward years later, and the facts start to unravel. The WMD narrative collapses. The intelligence was wrong. Fabricated. However you want to describe it. The result was the same.
Millions of Iraqis dead.
Trillions of taxpayer dollars spent.
More trillions in Afghanistan.
Twenty years of "war on" whatever slogan we needed to justify the next deployment.
And here we are decades later still asking: what exactly were we doing there?
Now I'm at the age where my age group is retiring after 20 - 30 years in the military. I meet more and more people who served in both Iraq and Afghanistan. If you work in healthcare, if you run for office, if you talk to veterans groups, VFW halls, disabled vet caucuses, you meet the people.
Some came back fine. Some didn't.
Some came back with skills.
Some came back with chronic back pain.
Some wake up in cold sweats.
Some drink too much.
Some can't maintain relationships.
Some never came home.
And let's be honest about who signs up.
It's not the elite class. It's not the politicians' kids. It's not hedge fund families. It's 18-year-olds from working-class neighborhoods staring at a $100,000 a year college bill, knowing they can't afford it, not wanting to drown in debt, and deciding the military is their only real shot at upward mobility.
They roll the dice with their lives because they feel they are too damn poor to have another option.
And then we sit here and tell ourselves this is just how it works.
We could fund affordable college.
We could build a stronger safety net.
We could create real opportunity without asking someone to risk PTSD or death for it.
Instead, we find the money for $100 million fighter jets. Every time.
_(p.s. I just heard bathrooms are leaking into the cafeteria at some of our Clevleand public schools that we cant fund so they have to eat in the gym). Whats the fix? 1/16th a jet? I digress._
This is what I call a scar on the national psyche.
Now, people say, "Why are Americans so anti-war? Why are they so reluctant? Why don't they support protecting America?"
Let's be clear. America has not had bombs falling on our cities in modern times. We haven't had neighborhoods flattened. We haven't watched our currency collapse because a foreign army rolled through our streets. My Russian friend has said that to me more than once. He says Americans really don't understand war because we haven't experienced it at home.
He's right about that part. We've been fortunate. Extremely fortunate. Privileged even. And I don't say that as an insult. I think everyone in the world deserves that level of security and comfort.
And it's very hard to make the case that it isn't because of our military actions.
But here's what we _do_ have.
We have the moral weight of knowing what our taxpayer dollars fund overseas.
We don't approve of bombs hitting schools.
We don't approve of toppling governments without clear justification tied directly to protecting American lives.
We don't approve of watching our brothers and sisters come home broken.
And we definitely don't approve of being told one thing during a campaign and shown another once power is secured.
This repetition leaves a mark.
Money in.
War out.
Veterans return changed.
Debt climbs.
The justification shifts.
That's not isolationism. That's pattern recognition.
There's a psychological tension in this country. We know we're powerful. We know we're wealthy. We know we're comfortable compared to much of the world. And at the same time, we know what our power projects abroad.
That tension creates guilt.
My stepfather worked for the same company for 42 years. It was employee-owned. The year he retired, it sold. His shares made him a millionaire overnight. He told me the guilt ate at him. His siblings were struggling. His kids were grinding. He didn't understand why he got lucky while others didn't.
I've heard similar stories from wealthy investors. They talk about guilt. About responsibility. About trying to give back not just out of generosity but out of discomfort.
Scale that up to a country.
We know we have it good.
We know we have power.
And we know that power has consequences.
We also know millions have died in conflicts funded by our taxes. Even if it sits in the back of our minds. Even if it's uncomfortable to say out loud.
That's collective trauma.
Not trauma from bombs on our soil.
Trauma from repetition.
From promises broken.
From trillions spent.
From watching the same cycle play out again and again.
People wonder why we don't have the same patriotic enthusiasm for military action that we had in World War II.
Because for decades what we've seen is not a clear existential fight on our shores. What we've seen is a rich country repeatedly spending billions -- tens of billions -- sometimes trillions -- projecting force into countries that cannot realistically fight back.
I'm not in intelligence briefings. I don't see classified memos. Maybe there are decisions made in back rooms that are more complex than we understand.
But I know what happens in living rooms.
People remember.
They remember Iraq.
They remember Afghanistan.
They remember being called crazy for opposing it.
They remember being proven right years later.
And until our leaders acknowledge that history and not spin it or rebrand it, they will continue to misread American reluctance.

## Dallas City Hall Fate Undecided
Following hours of public testimony and debate about the fate of Dallas City Hall, the city council voted 9-6 on Thursday to [explore options](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF4Zg9dQUKShe2lToll7wKMM9srMLo-_jzbKH6Q-0tG959fX8gXElLefsOMk32tZMp4HowjWJcD-3K9DKCSESnlLtKV3EVyssXdtOm3uSwTia-mbOD1MHNsGp9Z768fBed-kaYXg2t4BONMH4_o4uHHt17A-IAytg4amj8x05t5aY5272eB7P2AbfTTDCEH1BiNJqTdJKPgNx8pXeWO9hbI3PCWR56G6H8rOys7ned7yI8T1_GBl588fZWcuAVjZOQIzHDqQXDoBs654FH4JlawFfuM_FMorB2Id8QGCmrIUjVD50nupmfKmU3nVj7gbx67rRmXnpk7xeRIzHXeverPtQPx3pPxf2vdk_wQAAP__jtWQXA) to redevelop and repair the downtown site. Around 90 speakers addressed the council, which voted on the measure after 1 a.m. The council directed city staff to develop a plan to address critical repairs, relocate 311 and 911 services and emergency operations, and move out altogether. The measure bans contractors that helped produce a report that pegged the price of repairs at more than $1 billion from bidding on projects. Many of the speakers opposed abandoning City Hall and [urged the council](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAURL8GM60LgmhAsInZbLqhhXAVqlCm4O44_v3W7Ht_8OLu6q5z_jyWh40pnvtve6Ch95aXE6-akAjL4uzxPO5K0QW0JZ57iHt4ZcJFgBha6FsYFm9juhfZeLOCn3iDhmst9DQqrZtgUKoBwfJR6InzcVPrtK6ud6PfkHPvmmg-Y9DDwAUIpTrhtNQjcq89jJN1TAL6SLl0FJDwbeuW7vzC0rl8NMkEomdl_S8mZibm67o6b1OyNa8Vy3eNifnDxcT8lbUu0t0Gm1JbsOb0l2I-WwmDAgmKibkpxj-vmFKsg2YS9sPG9P-QfqbpZcS_AAAA__-kDX0X) to take a measured and transparent approach to future plans for the site. "_This is likely the biggest, most impactful, most expensive decision you may ever make in your career_ ," Preservation Dallas Executive Director Sarah Crain said. Others said the current structure, designed by famed architect I.M. Pei, doesn’t serve the city's current needs. "_Dallas deserves a City Hall that serves the next 50 years, not one that struggles under the weight of the last 50_ ," [said Sana Syed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O4yAUhZ_G7oiA2OAUFGnczbS7nXUD1wYtPxbcxOO3XyWvMN2RjvTpnO_P1_IFIYa8fUNCQz9rWTIeLSIR1sVC2tPZKFiPUEPefNj8qxAukkvF-JVxtTgI8VyG3pkHdzfRoxFaS32bRq17b9RNc7cKsGLVfBJXK9Q4TFpNCkb1ENAH84bxK1dCcjmOF2n1oCcUTjs-3cB2A0cXqNQLeST8gbbGs7ywXmxJfTSeaG_d9d7JuZPzcRyX1PK76-SMmT1bJ-f3qU7OnwwrYWUJKpAvmSVECnljDmKExmx5Zhsie4D915gNdDIPMbJUXsgaPd3JKu4QKtsj5Deusvtd_D2-3dpX4_YjxBia0t3AtwQhflbS79y-jPwfAAD__7Zyj_Y) of the Dallas Farmers Market Stakeholders Association.

name: Justin Streiff, Turning Point USA
subject: The book Charlie left behind
body:
Please read the message below from our sponsor.
* * *
| | | [](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)
---
| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn’t a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal — the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God’s grace.**

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**“God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”**_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)
---
When you read it, you will hear Charlie’s voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie’s hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

**[To claim your copy of this life-changing book, simply make a generous gift in any amount to Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)**
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA**
**& Receive Charlie’s Final Book**](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)
---
In the months since Charlie’s assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA’s message among young Americans...

...and it’s not just the conservative message as a whole — _**it’s the message of FAITH!**_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie’s call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it’s happening._

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we’re witnessing is not just growth —**it’s revival.**

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America’s faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up.**

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _“We’re not backing down.”_

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie’s most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie’s faith._**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

**[To claim your copy of Charlie’s final book, simply make a gift, in any amount, to support Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)**
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA**
**& Receive Charlie’s Final Book**](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)
---
I’ll personally ensure your copy is sent to you as soon as possible.

Thank you in advance for carrying on Charlie’s mission and supporting his legacy.
---
**For Charlie,**

**Justin Streiff**
Chief Operating Officer
Turning Point USA
---
[](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)
---
**[Support Turning Point USA](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)**
---
**P.S.** When you read **_Stop, in the Name of God,_** you will discover what Charlie found in the Sabbath: a holy rest that steadies the heart, renews the soul, and gives strength for the road ahead.

**[I hope you’ll claim your copy by making your most generous gift to Turning Point USA. Your support fuels our work to build the most faithful generation of Americans in history. Thank you, and God bless!](https://trk.rightwingreport.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbh937&__onlt=h)**

| Letter from the Chair
---
A Night to Remember: Honoring Our State Senators at the NEGOP Recognition Dinner
Dear Fellow Republicans,
Last night was truly special--a powerful evening of gratitude, fellowship, and shared purpose.
Twenty-eight State Senators, many accompanied by their spouses, gathered with us at the Nebraska Republican Party's annual Senator Recognition Dinner to celebrate service, leadership, and the momentum we're building together.
The evening kicked off with a heartfelt VIP reception honoring those serving their final session in the Legislature:

* Speaker John Arch, LD 14
* Senator Christy Armendariz, LD 18
* Senator Tom Brandt, LD 32
* Senator Rob Clements, LD 2
* Senator Myron Dorn, LD 30
* Senator Ben Hansen, LD 16
* Senator Mike Moser, LD 22
* Senator Dave Murman, LD 38

These dedicated public servants have given so much to our state--we're proud to have honored them.
The main program opened with solemn reflection:
Senator Rick Holdcroft, LD 36 led a moment of silence for our fallen heroes, including Nebraska's own Sergeant First Class Noah L. Tietjens, a 42-year-old Army Reserve soldier from Bellevue who made the ultimate sacrifice. He followed with a moving invocation.
Senator Loren Lippincott, LD 34 then led us proudly in the Pledge of Allegiance.
We presented well-deserved awards recognizing exceptional contributions to our party and state:
* Lifetime Achievement Award to the Honorable Donald Stenberg, presented by Attorney General Mike Hilgers
* Outstanding Legacy Statesman Award to the Honorable Carol McBride Pirsch, presented by Senator Kathleen Kauth (LD 31)
* Distinguished Service Award to Speaker John Arch, presented by Jeanne Reigle, NEGOP Director of Government Relations
* People's Choice for Exemplary Leadership to Senator Barry DeKay (LD 40), also presented by Jeanne Reigle

Speaker Arch took time to personally recognize every attending State Senator and spouse-- a touching moment that underscored the respect and camaraderie in the room.
We also extended appreciation to:
* Our brave military members and first responders
* Generous event sponsors
* Senators running for re-election
* Other candidates and their spouses in attendance
* More than 30 bright students from UNL, UNO, and Council Bluffs, representing the next generation of conservative leaders

The night wrapped up on a high note after a delicious dinner, filled with laughter and entertainment from nationally known comedian Tom Shillue, whose sharp wit offered levity to the evening.
A huge thank you to every sponsor, attendee, and especially our State Senators, statewide officeholders, and elected officials who joined us. Your presence and enthusiasm fueled an unforgettable celebration of service and unity.
Together, we win elections--and nights like this remind us why we fight so hard.

For Nebraska, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| Peter, The first big election for Democrats this year is here.
On April 7, Wisconsin voters will decide the future of their State Supreme Court. And with less than two months to go, the race is already exploding.
Last year, Democrats flipped the Wisconsin Supreme Court and secured a 4 to 3 majority. Now, with another seat up for grabs, we have a chance to expand that majority to 5 to 2.
If we win this race, Democrats could lock down control of this critical swing state court until at least 2030.
That means protecting voting rights. Protecting reproductive freedom. Protecting democracy itself in one of the most important battleground states in the country.
And the race has officially begun.
Liberal Judge Chris Taylor just launched the first major ad campaign of the race, warning that extremist judges like her MAGA opponent Maria Lazar are coming for basic benefits like BadgerCare and even trying to enforce Wisconsin's 1849 abortion ban.
Within days, Lazar fired back with a six figure ad blitz of her own calling Taylor a radical and absurdly claiming she wants non-citizens to vote.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001f8-k4s_zp0qlmI18lA48znxbPUUEZIrprmqz0itmlulowt1dxJWPgFhL5Yo8VDWIb5uj5KyiB7p-CLJ8tVBJ4rM66cnNmVFzRKoV056KlIXLFeQF008ZCaPRtf6oaK9AyENTM0uWbXccn-jrNaVorpAcQCU6hej82RRldESCrarPGVMob-qL54XvyQpyUwS2ghx6LTDJoAeTQoE6dkKBiWPCT1rP0-WhNDpdANJODLY=&c=Qa-cHnpuHo5rbOdZX4Jq4-S7pg5DiVx_IC1nt7oACTyhMjuxMm-2sg==&ch=jfAnF0xRFrIkpix7zFBhrwcmne1ZRziTgs6QF2Fz4RHwt4242LoaQQ==)
---
The first shots of this race have been fired. It's now a dead sprint to the finish.
Right now, Taylor has the edge in fundraising, outraising Lazar by 10-1. But we don't expect this edge to last long. MAGA billionaires and dark money groups will be jumping in the race any day now to prop up Lazar and attack Taylor.
That's why Defend Our Courts is jumping in to help Wisconsin Democrats defeat Lazar. But we need to move fast to be prepared for the inevitable onslaught of MAGA cash, disinformation, and smears.
Last year, we helped lead the successful defense of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, locking in a Democratic majority there until 2029. Now, we are taking our winning formula national.
Wisconsin is our first major test of 2026.

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | 220 Executive Orders in just one year. | And with nearly three full years left on the clock... In our last email, we discussed how hyper-nationalism sets the stage for authoritarianism. Today, we look at the second sign of fascism: **The Disregard for Human Rights.** Fascist regimes frequently persuade the public that human rights can be ignored in specific cases of "external threats" or for "national security." That’s why it’s so vital that we conduct our own polling, especially when there’s a discrepancy with the numbers like what we’re seeing right now. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. Null, it’s Haley, and I had to email you because the House voted on the SAVE America Act a few weeks ago – legislation that would make it MUCH more difficult for millions of people to vote, including women who are married and changed their last names, disabled people, people without passports, people who have lost their birth certificates, and many more.
This is part of a Republican effort to end voting by mail.

Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and their MAGA minions desperately want to pass this legislation – and as someone who deeply cares about the voting rights of ALL Americans and the future of our democracy, I couldn’t be more strongly opposed.
But I need to know that you’re with me, null. So will you please take 10 seconds to be one of the 100 poll responses I need from 18326 before midnight?

| | Recently, a supporter who has been involved in Knoxville politics for decades said something that stuck with me: _“I usually see the same 40 people at political events. But when I come to yours, the room is full of people I’ve never seen before.”_ The same thing happened last weekend at the [Knox Young Democrats](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/HmMFn2bhUmZzkGV0n6ueAw~~/AAUS1hA~/oxf0jIgj9b4yhbGiyD6c0U2B9mmULkQsGxszDCxgPw6neeiXOUH097oa_uG3YUpMlNBrcEQEuUgwbTIZpE_mDo35V6mkf-VZz-AlYt4VEGmYpzPL_oa1x0go8cmyOvO0)’ packed launch event. There were so many new people in the room. Folks who “didn’t do politics” but now see that politics has been doing them. _*Photo credit: Saturn and Sun Collective_ Standing room only, new faces everywhere. **The makings of a movement.** The uphill battle we face is no secret. I’m running in the longest-held Republican district in the country against an incumbent who regularly wins nearly 70% of the vote. Some folks say they’d rather spend their time and money somewhere that feels more “winnable.” I understand that calculation, but it makes me wonder, “When _is_ the right time to invest if we ever want this to feel possible?” **History shows us the fights that seemed unwinnable are the ones that changed our country.** The fight against AIDS. The Civil Rights Act. The Americans with Disabilities Act. Marriage equality. Activists didn’t wait for the perfect moment. They showed up, organized, and **created the conditions for change**. We know the cavalry isn’t coming for us ... We are the cavalry. If you believe in this movement we are building something in East Tennessee, [chip in what you can today.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/VqhNH92U9lK7xQDFXcU1Ug~~/AAUS1hA~/L6dTx7xiu3x5dBb-qn06u6N4k7mqzLOR4m8F-i-ngJ2pNVwX86Ls1lDTg36Q-JszlZ-Tu_7UqE2f7oUSRfoq7E8h6HDcguJN46s2jcL2y6ylX_i-rv_5NqaydGtjCHt4hBxXkSSo1jt0CewLb7g72A9G9q0uJNv7jf8yyDpBwZw~) And if you'd like to listen to my full remarks from the Knox Young Dems launch, you can do so [here](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/QWPYFgXu0DME7a05NdsqYw~~/AAUS1hA~/VHAdZenouBWh1V_ThbYHWgJ5zAbBOkwlmZ6UbCXU3b4uwzbP6dMw0YtMmab6P1ylIz7W9EUEShWST6uVtAduYbuB8xvRrlp8JUpXSGylsv1Jx2FgjE-X3AY8Z9a0w3TUC6JOwjexpnC8rGQ9eVW2rQ~~). clean_body: A long-time political force in Knoxville politics told me... | | | Recently, a supporter who has been involved in Knoxville politics for decades said something that stuck with me: “I usually see the same 40 people at political events. But when I come to yours, the room is full of people I’ve never seen before.” The same thing happened last weekend at the ’ packed launch event. There were so many new people in the room. Folks who “didn’t do politics” but now see that politics has been doing them. Photo credit: Saturn and Sun Collective Standing room only, new faces everywhere. The makings of a movement. The uphill battle we face is no secret. I’m running in the longest-held Republican district in the country against an incumbent who regularly wins nearly 70% of the vote. Some folks say they’d rather spend their time and money somewhere that feels more “winnable.” I understand that calculation, but it makes me wonder, “When is the right time to invest if we ever want this to feel possible?” History shows us the fights that seemed unwinnable are the ones that changed our country. The fight against AIDS. The Civil Rights Act. The Americans with Disabilities Act. Marriage equality. Activists didn’t wait for the perfect moment. They showed up, organized, and created the conditions for change**. We know the cavalry isn’t coming for us ... We are the cavalry. If you believe in this movement we are building something in East Tennessee, ~ And if you'd like to listen to my full remarks from the Knox Young Dems launch, you can do so ~~. body:

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/NPP_Ed_logo_RGB_green1-01.jpg]
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.
Upcoming events
As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Pittsburgh%20School%20board%20forum%208.5x11.png]
Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students.
Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader.
With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.
