#GoVotePA
SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [https://www.instagram.com/p/DJbyV6DPLdJ/]
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/DelCo_2.png] We are hiring!
Let's provide civic education together!
We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania.
Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote!
Positions start at $20 an hour.
Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org]
EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org]
News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]
* Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections/assistant/]
* Everything you need to know about mail voting [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-mail-ballot-how-to-request-fill-out-return] , becoming a poll worker [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide]
* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]
* Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-commonwealth-superior-court-candidates] , vetting judicial candidates [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-candidate-vetting-guide]
* Guides to State College school board [https://www.spotlightpa.org/statecollege/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-state-college-school-board-anderson-huff-barlow-black-desmarais-mcternan-sogor] , Reading City Council president [https://www.spotlightpa.org/berks/2025/04/reading-city-council-president-primary-election-2025]
* Guides to voting as a college student [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-college-student-voting-guide]
En Español
* Guía para votar por correo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pensilvania-elecciones-primarias-2025-votar-correo-como-llenar] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/reading-concejo-municipal-primarias-elecciones-2025]
* Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-primarias-elecciones-2025-votar-informacion] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-elecciones-2025-como-convertirse-trabajador-electoral]
2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. Upcoming events As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls. [] Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students. Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader. With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] [] Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot. Your vote shapes our justice system! Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms. When: Monday, May 12, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] Social Media of the Week [] The deadline to request your mail-in ballot for the primary election is May 13th at 5PM. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [] The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests. In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: U.S. Actions In Iran Are Impacting the Economy
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
What happens in the Middle East doesn’t stay in the Middle East.
The Price of Gas Is Up
Roughly 15% of the world's oil and 20% of its liquefied natural gas passes through the Strait of Hormuz, a single narrow choke point in the mouth of the Persian Gulf, so any disruption there is immediately a global problem. Everyday about 80 oil and gas tankers [https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/03/03/business/iran-war-oil-gas-strait-of-hormuz.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share] pass through. On Tuesday, just one appeared to pass through, according to the New York Times. The strait is essentially a corridor for the entire global economy, not just Middle Eastern countries, which is why a conflict there reverberates instantly in gas prices, stock markets, and shipping costs everywhere from New York to Tokyo.
Oil jumped around 6% [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/03/02/oil-prices-strait-hormuz/] to $75.22 a barrel in a single afternoon, diesel even more sharply at 14%, with analysts projecting pump prices could rise over 20 cents per gallon within the week
The $100/barrel threshold [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/jpmorgan-energy-guru-warns-oil-172634151.html] is the alarm bell analysts are watching nervously for.
As the Times reported, “Shipping companies have paused their tankers to protect their crew and cargo, and because insurance companies are charging significantly more to cover vessels in the conflict area.”
The New York Times created a visual representation of shipping activity in Strait of Hormuz below:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/Iran.png]
Global Markets Are Falling
On Tuesday, the Dow fell more than 400 points [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/iran-war-fears-markets-oil-surges-stocks-plunge-rcna261479] , while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both closed down around 1% — though at their worst point in the session the Dow had plunged over 1,200 points and the Nasdaq was down nearly 3%. The sell-off was global: Germany's DAX tumbled 3.6%, Italy fell nearly 4%, Spain dropped 4.5%, and South Korea's Kospi plummeted 7%. Europe's broad Stoxx 600 index slid more. For the year in 2026, the Dow has fallen over 2% and fallen into negative territory.
War Is Expensive
There is nothing more costly than when we lose one of our service members. We’ve heartbreaking lost six so far - and while less than 1% of our nation serves actively in the military - we all must continue to keep them and all the people in the Middle East in our prayers. Remember to separate the war from our warriors, it’s the political leaders in Washington DC that sent them there.
A new report from the Center for American Progress [https://www.americanprogress.org/article/the-trump-administrations-reckless-war-in-iran-has-already-cost-more-than-5-billion/] estimates that Trump’s military actions in Iran have cost American taxpayers more than $5 billion in just the first days of the conflict. That number is likely an undercount, since it doesn't include a $1.1 billion U.S. radar system Iran allegedly destroyed in Qatar or the full cost of missile interceptors already fired. Just running two aircraft carrier groups and associated air power is costing an estimated $60 million per day [https://ips-dc.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Iran-War-Costs-Operation-Epic-Fury.pdf] .
Each Patriot missile costs around $4 million [https://responsiblestatecraft.org/iran-war-costs/] and there are reports of up to 11 being fired to intercept a single Iranian missile. With hundreds of Iranian missiles intercepted so far, the tab on interceptors alone runs into the billions.
The Pentagon is now reportedly preparing an emergency funding request of up to $50 billion [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/defense-executives-plan-meet-white-house-strikes-iran-diminish-stockpiles-2026-03-04/] to replace munitions and equipment. It’s a mechanism critics compare to the post-9/11 "Overseas Contingency Operations" fund that ultimately exceeded $2 trillion for the Iraq and Afghanistan wars, largely outside normal congressional oversight.
For my in depth perspective on the conflict with Iran, you can read my latest Substack. [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/p/unpacking-the-us-israel-strikes-on] I’ve been on Fox, ABC News, BBC and Great Britian news this week. Here’s one of our most recent clips [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/patrickmurphypa_politics-ends-at-the-waters-edge-that-activity-7434985658118721536-FdiY?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_ios&rcm=ACoAADKsKswB4R3Ni7hN4W3mL_7SGAh8ViWRArE] . Thank you for being part of our team.
Be sure to follow me on Instagram and subscribe to my Substack for my weekly geopolitical and business analysis.
- Patrick
Be sure to follow me on Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/patrickmurphypa/?hl=en] and subscribe to my Substack [https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa] for my weekly geopolitical and business analysis .

Bush, Washington tried to brand governments hostile to U.S. interests--namely Iran, Iraq, and North Korea--as an "[axis of evil](https://substack.com/redirect/8afd322a-34a1-4237-b421-09e9ce811f85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Today, the term is much appropriately applied to the U.S. and Israel.
They are the only two countries in the world to [embrace](https://substack.com/redirect/e8086aef-33dc-4f1d-8e94-34e122e1494e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the ongoing genocide in Gaza, the only two countries to [reject](https://substack.com/redirect/bad6e7e2-68ca-4926-9fc0-fb6f4052e3c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a proposed global right to food, and the two international antagonists that together [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/35024509-85ae-49df-a529-4f7c2985a74d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the war on Iran that has killed hundreds of children while sparking shocks across the global supply chain.
American belligerence towards the rest of the world has been shamelessly consistent, long predating the attack on Iran that began last week. America has been at (usually undeclared, yet all-too-real) war for [most of its existence](https://substack.com/redirect/37b8c1c2-aabd-4770-aa93-2429f3de78e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), while--particularly since the end of the Second World War--[most of the rest of the world](https://substack.com/redirect/6c527bb6-b354-4751-ba8f-3f71033e6850?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has come under fire directed from Washington.
Despite America's notorious disdain for human rights both abroad and within our own country, Europe has largely remained committed to Washington's foreign policy objectives. European countries [bleated](https://substack.com/redirect/7b0bbb1d-1cb5-49fa-a25e-82d8eec60703?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about American hegemony when Trump threatened Greenland, only to conspicuously [line up behind him](https://substack.com/redirect/ffccf3c9-ed72-4287-b866-cc1084392238?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when his sights shifted to Iran.
_Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a publication made possible by readers, rather than advertisers. To receive new posts,**sign up for a free subscription!** To support my work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0mKXBlhDovbpR8DdTy32e16FUf2EOORfJ2f3vX9VfV4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=190083576)
The continent's obsequious deference to Trump's madness is almost as revolting as the way Democrats have [paved](https://substack.com/redirect/ab6d0670-fa8a-4676-8a0c-374f31751b10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his path.
The mania enabling this war is not confined to Washington, but is in fact widely shared across western governments. Their hypocrisy is as sickening as it is predictable.
It seems as if [Spain](https://substack.com/redirect/7c952a2a-9a87-4d9b-a8cc-0498b5a6cbfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is the one country in Europe that has any awareness of history. And just to be clear, I don't mean the longstanding history of American belligerence since the Second World War. A [memory of 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/364ced07-9207-4ff0-be9f-6b851d5f7ce9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) should be enough for Europe to recognize its interests.
### **Blood in the Water**
Trump fired Kristi Noem from her position as DHS Secretary not because he wanted to, or because she lost his favor--but because GOP Senators could no longer ignore her brutality, lies, and willingness to antagonize the public.
The proximate cause of Noem's long overdue dismissal wasn't her lies on national television characterizing peaceful, law-abiding Good Samaritan as "domestic terrorists," but rather her [advertising deal](https://substack.com/redirect/a0c39ba3-e943-464f-95b3-59a6f35a5c11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with a former staffer's company.
Yesterday, a U.S. Marine [disrupted](https://substack.com/redirect/ca60ae80-5538-4d45-832e-23085a7c3bbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Senate proceeding to declare that ""America does not want to send its sons and daughters to war for Israel!," before a U.S. Senator broke his arm whistle forcibly removing him from the chamber.
Having been [arrested myself in 2015](https://substack.com/redirect/844e3d20-0483-4075-9ae6-6c5f9745b5f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for speaking after the conclusion of a Senate hearing to pose a question that no one in elected office has the independence to raise, it saddens me that elected chickenhawks are allowed to inflict injury on servicemembers who understand the Constitution better than they do.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=190083576&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwMDgzNTc2LCJpYXQiOjE3NzI4MTAwOTYsImV4cCI6MTc3NTQwMjA5NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.DX88Nru-duuFw6EBStgR5BxJeqGt7kREFbDof3OUgUk)
Americans across the political continuum are clamoring for sanity in U.S. foreign policy. It might not be long before Secretary of War Hegseth meets the same fate as Noem. The one thing one can say for Hegseth is that he tore the mask off U.S. foreign policy, making clear that the pretense of "defense" was always a twisted joke.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio's [admission](https://substack.com/redirect/24b42208-a47c-434c-b35e-1072a9e6f37c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Trump followed Netanyahu's lead was a crucial revelation. If European countries still wield any independence, or harbor any self-respect, they will defect from the new Axis of Evil and instead support the human rights principles that the U.S. has overtly abandoned and consistently violated both [at home](https://substack.com/redirect/aed6079f-3015-453b-87b3-8eeb8c76510e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [abroad](https://substack.com/redirect/3d0ac06e-e622-4bf4-8522-cce5af71b51b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
### **Is Washington falling into a trap of its own making?**
To this point, interceptor missiles have limited the damage done by Iran's notorious fleet of drones and missiles.
But, as many commenters have [observed](https://substack.com/redirect/0e4ef190-0e22-41ee-817c-1313cb0abc17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Iran can build drones for around $20,000 that the U.S. and Israel are spending millions to intercept. Iran builds these drones en masse, and quickly, whereas building an advanced interceptor missile used by the U.S. can take [over a year](https://substack.com/redirect/2a703105-d9b1-4c17-a0a4-67590e8b6085?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
From this perspective, Trump's attack on Tehran may have been a colossal miscalculation. Why would anyone be surprised, given how [little thought](https://substack.com/redirect/0ea59be1-4012-468c-9d6a-c11ca10222f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) apparently went into the strike in the first place?

### **One job should be enough**
Long on its heels in the face of predation by Wall Street, [organized labor in the U.S.](https://substack.com/redirect/f7775060-cb23-43b4-983c-8ba3d8f061d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has experienced a remarkable [resurgence](https://substack.com/redirect/3cc3bdf8-c1d2-482b-9c80-f0d76c3c8ae8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in recent years. Among the movement's most popular slogans is one that will resonate with anyone juggling multiple side gigs and projects in order to survive: "One job should be enough."
I reflect on that slogan because I recently sat down to count the number of projects I pursue in order to make ends meet, and discovered even more than I had previously realized. While I felt grateful to have forged a 20-year career in public advocacy before running for office, the character assassination that [ended](https://substack.com/redirect/d4f21d4a-1ece-419f-ba94-d098344fd150?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that phase of my life forced me to pursue half a dozen different paid projects in order to survive:
1. The closest thing I have to a full-time job is working as a snowboard instructor in the winter.
2. In the summer, my outdoor mountain job shifts to kayak guiding, which includes offering ecology and history tours.
3. I work year-round as a DJ, both in nightclubs and for private events like weddings.
4. About a year ago, I started teaching capoeira at a local gym.
5. My vestigial legal practice includes co-representing a series of tenants across the Bay Area in struggles against (mostly corporate) landlords.
6. Finally, I write this column, from which I earn a bit less than $500/month.

I'll be honest with you: I can't keep up with the news cycle.
There was a time in my life when I had the luxury of dedicating my time to informing the public. I no longer enjoy that privilege, which is one reason why I publish far less frequently than I wish.
If you're reading this, and have learned anything from my analysis of [law](https://substack.com/redirect/65fc0e2a-2898-4fa2-ac7f-93638427af76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [politics](https://substack.com/redirect/b7a04bcd-d9e2-4a35-a65b-cedecfe24f12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [history](https://substack.com/redirect/87028886-57ac-4c39-a6af-269a0ef8e522?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [culture](https://substack.com/redirect/6c9108fa-7a1c-4fde-85e4-d50d45f2569d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I implore you to consider becoming a paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0mKXBlhDovbpR8DdTy32e16FUf2EOORfJ2f3vX9VfV4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=190083576)
That invitation feels only more poignant having recently discovered evidence of my algorithmic suppression on this platform.
### **Is Substack hiding insightful writers from readers?**
Earlier this week, I posted [a Note](https://substack.com/@shahidbuttar/note/c-222450135?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios&utm_source=notes-share-action) on the Substack app quoting a passage from [a post](https://substack.com/redirect/3d0ac06e-e622-4bf4-8522-cce5af71b51b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) I wrote about a month ago, in the wake of Trump's attack on Venezuela. Across my audience of over 20,000 subscribers, that post attracted 6 likes and 2 restacks.
Another author--whose voice I very much appreciate--[quoted](https://substack.com/@longdefiant/note/c-222456074?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios&utm_source=notes-share-action) my note and added a short, supportive preceding reflection. With an audience of 263 subscribers, their post drew 19 likes, 8 replies, and 4 restacks.
A publication with roughly 1.6% of my readers received more than 300% greater engagement on a post that was substantially the same.
It does not surprise me that my work is made less visible to potential new readers than that of other writers. It does, however, surprise me to see such a lopsided disparity between the (vastly narrower) visibility of my work and that of other authors quoting me.
All that is to say, the suppression of my voice leaves me all the more reliant on readers to share my writing in other fora, whether the Substack app, or Instagram, or Facebook, or BlueSky.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=190083576&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwMDgzNTc2LCJpYXQiOjE3NzI4MTAwOTYsImV4cCI6MTc3NTQwMjA5NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.DX88Nru-duuFw6EBStgR5BxJeqGt7kREFbDof3OUgUk)
If you're not yet a paid subscriber, please consider supporting a marginalized voice with a [history](https://substack.com/redirect/7e41b3dc-ba54-4268-8848-8eb88e34c0b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of both anticipating our country's most severe social challenges, and [stepping forward](https://substack.com/redirect/cf82e813-8ad4-4085-88f3-c33842ab9ecb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to propose alternatives despite the severe risk in speaking out as a dissident of color.
Having dedicated decades of my life to alerting a largely ignorant public, I remain committed to the work that institutional journalism has effectively abandoned. As a lone voice juggling half a dozen jobs, however, I can't do it without support from readers.

# Kicking Off Our Campaign By Outraising Our Opponent 5:1 in February!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/QOYgs5aBFGo?e=62156fa6a8&c2id=b6a5a472a55a2c2f8f90113ea210fcd0)
| | Our campaign has hit the ground running across the district — from participating in the Wetumpka Mardi Gras Parade to attending community meetings to dialing for dollars.
The good news: our hard work is already paying off. In February, we raised $25,000 and outraised our Republican opponent 5:1 — proof that this campaign is building real momentum and that people across District 26 are ready for leadership that will show up, listen, and do the work.
At the same time, our opponent still has nearly $500,000 in the bank from special interests and PACs. That means we have to keep building the grassroots support needed to get our message out and connect with voters across District 26 about what is at stake in this race.
**Will you join our campaign and help us close the gap? The people of District 26 deserve a Senator who will work for them — not for special interests.**
---
| [Help Me Close the Gap!](https://us.list-manage.com/sG1Owdlazuz?e=62156fa6a8&c2id=b6a5a472a55a2c2f8f90113ea210fcd0)
---
|
---
| |
# Recap: Mardi Gras in Wetumpka!
---
|
---
| | Even though our campaign has only been on the ballot for a month, we hit the streets for the Annual Mardi Gras Parade in Downtown Wetumpka.
Take a look at our custom Mardi Gras float — and thank you to all of the amazing volunteers who helped us make such a strong first impression.
---
|
---
| | [_**Join us for our campaign kick-off at 3:30 p.m. on March 21 at Montgomery Whitewater to meet future volunteers, connect as a community, and help grow our people-powered campaign!**_](https://us.list-manage.com/xGt__ibgcoU?e=62156fa6a8&c2id=b6a5a472a55a2c2f8f90113ea210fcd0)
---
| [Join our growing team!](https://us.list-manage.com/9EYPhnUw5kO?e=62156fa6a8&c2id=b6a5a472a55a2c2f8f90113ea210fcd0)
---
|
---
| |
# Honoring Selma’s Legacy
---
|
---
| | This weekend, our campaign will pause its usual schedule to join community members and civil rights leaders in Selma to commemorate Bloody Sunday. We do so with humility, honoring those who risked everything in the fight for voting rights and remembering the courage that changed Alabama — and our nation — forever.
It is an opportunity for reflection, remembrance, and gratitude, and we are honored to take part.

For more information, visit[ https://www.flippo4nv.com/](https://electdavidflippo.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9aba26b775663b53df718fc1a&id=fd9d6c5b8a&e=273c9a71fb) ###
About David
David Flippo is a battle-tested American patriot and strong leader with a proven record of problem-solving. As a retired Air Force combat commander, he led over 1,000 Airmen and established multiple operating bases during combat operations in Iraq. His military leadership extended to commanding maintenance squadrons responsible for dozens of combat aircraft in Alaska. After retiring, David applied his skills to the private sector, managing maintenance programs for BP’s Alaska oilfields, and now owns two small businesses in Nevada, where he understands firsthand the challenges of inflation, supply chain issues, and rising costs.
Nevada needs leaders like David who put people first by tackling surging crime, failing schools, burdensome regulations, and attacks on Constitutional freedoms. His experience in leadership and fiscal responsibility equips him to rein in government overreach and champion a servant leadership approach for all Nevadans. David Flippo is ready to fight for Nevada with courage and commitment. For more information, visit [flippo4nv.com](https://electdavidflippo.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9aba26b775663b53df718fc1a&id=4f60141d45&e=273c9a71fb)

It should come as no surprise that Florida is the example to emulate when it comes to states working with the federal government on immigration enforcement.
I was recently given a front row seat to see the partnership through a ride along with the Florida Highway Patrol. While FHP is not the only local law enforcement agency to work with ICE and Border Patrol to arrest illegal aliens in the state, they have certainly put in the work.
FHP has made around 9,000 arrests since March of last year. At the start of last week's operation, 1,567 of them had criminal histories beyond being in the U.S. illegally. All Florida law enforcement agencies have made over 20,000 arrests, thanks to their integration through ICE's 287(g) program near the start of President Trump's second term.
Governor Ron DeSantis signed a law that mandates all state and local police departments and sheriff's offices work with ICE beyond allowing access to jails and prisons.

What was remarkable is the stark difference between the environment in Florida as opposed to places like Minnesota and Illinois. The difference should come as no surprise considering Florida is a law and order state that has no sanctuary cities, but to see it up close after being in Minneapolis earlier this year was still shocking.
No one was speeding and chasing the FHP or ICE vehicles while honking their horns. When arrests were being made, no one was blowing whistles or interfering with the operation. Yes, people were filming while they were behind the wheel, but that was the extent of anything. Very few people shouted obscenities as they drove by.
To highlight how less hostile the operating environment is, even some ICE agents did not feel the need to wear face coverings. Using a mask is a must in Democrat-controlled areas since far-left activists will make sure to dox the federal agents if their faces are seen.

* Battery
* Burglary
* Possession and Conspiracy to Sell Heroin
* Firearm and Drug Trafficking
* Illegal Possession of a Firearm

**Friend — I want to tell you about a part of California I love deeply and a leader who is fighting like hell to protect it.** California’s 3rd Congressional District is one of the most breathtaking places in America — from the northern Sierra Nevada to the shores of Lake Tahoe to the vast beauty of Death Valley. It’s a region defined by its natural treasures. It’s also a region on the frontlines of the climate crisis. Extreme heat, severe drought, devastating wildfires, and rising flood risk are reshaping life in this district every single year. For families watching their wildfire insurance costs skyrocket or their neighbors losing homes to fires that burn hotter and longer each season, the climate crisis is no longer a distant threat. It is a direct danger to their safety and livelihoods. **[That's why I'm proud to announce JanePAC's endorsement of Heidi Hall for Congress in CA-03. Heidi is exactly the kind of leader I had in mind when I founded my Climate PAC.
_As a former EPA official,_ she spent years holding polluters accountable and protecting communities along the U.S.-Mexico border from hazardous waste and toxic dumping.
_As a three-term Nevada County Supervisor,_ she led the transition to electric vehicles, invested in solar power, and initiated her county's first-ever greenhouse gas emissions assessment.
And what makes Heidi the type of leader that gets me excited is that her love for our planet translates directly into her love for people: **Heidi called for Kristi Noem's impeachment and demands accountability for ICE agents who've brought terror into our communities.**
That’s what leadership looks like, friend — and boy do we have an incredible opportunity in front of us. New congressional maps approved by California voters under Proposition 50 have significantly shifted the political landscape in CA-03. This seat is now competitive and winnable. But Heidi must first win a tough primary, and early resources will make all the difference.

clean_body: This seat can help us flip the House. | Friend — I want to tell you about a part of California I love deeply and a leader who is fighting like hell to protect it. California’s 3rd Congressional District is one of the most breathtaking places in America — from the northern Sierra Nevada to the shores of Lake Tahoe to the vast beauty of Death Valley. It’s a region defined by its natural treasures. It’s also a region on the frontlines of the climate crisis. Extreme heat, severe drought, devastating wildfires, and rising flood risk are reshaping life in this district every single year. For families watching their wildfire insurance costs skyrocket or their neighbors losing homes to fires that burn hotter and longer each season, the climate crisis is no longer a distant threat. It is a direct danger to their safety and livelihoods. = | = Heidi is exactly the kind of leader I had in mind when I founded my Climate PAC. As a former EPA official, she spent years holding polluters accountable and protecting communities along the U.S.-Mexico border from hazardous waste and toxic dumping. As a three-term Nevada County Supervisor, she led the transition to electric vehicles, invested in solar power, and initiated her county's first-ever greenhouse gas emissions assessment. And what makes Heidi the type of leader that gets me excited is that her love for our planet translates directly into her love for people: Heidi called for Kristi Noem's impeachment and demands accountability for ICE agents who've brought terror into our communities. That’s what leadership looks like, friend — and boy do we have an incredible opportunity in front of us. New congressional maps approved by California voters under Proposition 50 have significantly shifted the political landscape in CA-03. This seat is now competitive and winnable. subject: Our opponents are gearing up to go on the attack and spend millions lying about me on TV
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
Addressing the rumors...
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/101102?refcode=em20260306-10141&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10141%2E614464%2EP9KjcR)
Peter,
The past few weeks, I keep hearing rumors that political operatives who are part of the DC corporate establishment are calling our donors, our supporters, and our endorsers – trying to strong arm them into no longer supporting our campaign and blunt our momentum.
**It’s clear: Our opponents in DC – the corporate PACs, billionaire Super PACs, AIPAC, and the political establishment machine – are gearing up to go on the attack and spend millions lying about me on TV.**
I refuse to take their money or do their bidding. And that scares them. They’d rather have Susan Collins or another milquetoast establishment Democrat they can count on than someone wiling to stand up and fight the fascists trying to destroy our democracy.
I served four infantry tours in Iraq and Afghanistan. I’m not afraid of millions of dollars in TV ads lying about me. I knew the fight I signed up for when I decided to run against Susan Collins and take on the entire DC political establishment.
We are going to defeat Susan Collins and flip Maine’s Senate seat blue with a Democrat who isn’t afraid of a fight this November. Susan Collins is the most vulnerable Republican senator in the entire country – but the polls show this is an extremely close race right now.
I’m not taking money from corporate PACs or AIPAC – and for that reason, we rely entirely on small-dollar contributions from people like you to fund our campaign. **I’m ready to take on Susan Collins and all of the DC corporate Super PACs, but I need your help now if we’re going to do it.**
**[So I am once again asking: Please, can I count on you to split a donation right now between our campaign and Heartland Patriots to help me defeat Susan Collins, flip Maine blue, and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/101102?refcode=em20260306-10141&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10141%2E614464%2EP9KjcR)**
There’s no amount of money these oligarchs can spend that’s ever going to make me back down from fighting for working-class Mainers.
It’s you and me versus Susan Collins and the billionaires.
In solidarity,
Graham Platner

Peter,
FIRST: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth tried to strong-arm Anthropic into opening its AI for unrestricted military use.
THEN: Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, drew two clear red lines: No mass domestic surveillance of Americans. No fully autonomous AI weapons.
NOW: The Trump administration has retaliated. Donald Trump ordered [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/27/us/politics/anthropic-military-ai.html?campaign_id=60&emc=edit_na_20260227&instance_id=171760&nl=breaking-news&regi_id=53717295&segment_id=215918&user_id=4f8ecc30d44042290b7b9c00f416abaa] federal agencies to phase out Anthropic’s technology rather than respect basic guardrails.
Let’s be clear about what this fight is really about.
Hegseth wants AI systems with no limits.
No limits on surveillance.
No limits on automation in war.
No limits on a $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget that supercharges a war-and-surveillance machine.
That is unacceptable.
I’m calling on Congress to act immediately:
✅ Ban Pentagon AI contractors from spying on Americans.
✅ Prohibit fully autonomous AI warfare – there must always be a human decision-maker when America goes to war.
✅ Protect AI companies that refuse to build tools for domestic repression.
✅ Reject Trump’s reckless $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget and invest in healthcare, housing, childcare, and good-paying jobs at home instead.
And I’m thanking Anthropic for modeling moral responsibility when it mattered.
Will you join me?

Derek, we’re reaching out because you’re one of our most reliable supporters, and we were hoping you could help us out. **We’re in a little bit of a pickle this month. Here’s why:** With Primary Day just over two months away, we expected to see a big jump in grassroots donations compared to last month. But we haven’t. Instead, donations are trending _downward._ [_**If this continues, this would be a BIG problem, Derek. We’re about to hold a big finance meeting over the weekend, and we’ll be honest: There could be some serious budget cuts if this trend doesn’t change.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126790889/605965424/1751931448?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&refcode=email_030626_inapickle&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZjE1NGE5Ni03OTE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4Zxj38sRrqsyPr9DQNRL3lNFrCtWkCivAIMRymfgbmg=) | | [Donate →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126790891/605965425/1751931448?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&refcode=email_030626_inapickle&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZjE1NGE5Ni03OTE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4Zxj38sRrqsyPr9DQNRL3lNFrCtWkCivAIMRymfgbmg=)

In 2016, Donald Trump won Pennsylvania by just one percentage point.
In 2020, Joe Biden won our Commonwealth by just one percentage point.
And in 2024? Republicans won a Senate seat by **just 0.22%.**
Again and again, Pennsylvania’s elections come down to just a small handful of votes — votes that are earned only through extensive organizing, statewide ad buys, and dozens of in-person events.
So yes, Derek — lots and lots of people have chipped in since Launch Day. And we can’t even begin to tell you how grateful we are for that support. But elections in Pennsylvania aren’t decided by which candidate has the momentum in March.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMarch 6, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**State Representative Roger Wilder Endorses Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate**
**BATON ROUGE, LA** \- Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the only candidate in the race endorsed by President Trump, announced she has received the endorsement of State Representative Roger Wilder in her campaign for the United States Senate. Wilder joins a growing coalition of conservative leaders across Louisiana in endorsing Letlow’s campaign for the United States Senate.
Representative Wilder, who represents Louisiana’s 71st District, cited Rep. Letlow’s consistent conservative record and commitment to Louisiana families as key reasons for his support.
_“Congresswoman Julia Letlow has demonstrated principled leadership and a deep commitment to the people of Louisiana,”_**said Rep. Wilder**. _“She has been a reliable vote for conservative values in Congress, earned the endorsement of President Trump, and has delivered real results for our state. Louisiana needs a senator who will stand firm when the pressure is on, and I believe Julia is the right leader for this moment.”_
Letlow’s Trump-endorsed campaign is focused on keeping the border secure, strengthening American energy production, protecting parental rights in education, and lowering costs for hardworking families.
_“I’m truly grateful for Representative Wilder’s support,”_**said Rep. Letlow**. _“Roger has been a strong voice for his district and for conservative principles in our state. I look forward to continuing to work alongside leaders like him as we build a campaign focused on delivering for Louisiana.”_
Rep. Letlow currently serves on the House Education and the Workforce Committee and the House Appropriations Committee, and has helped return hundreds of millions of dollars to Louisiana taxpayers.
For more information, visit [JuliaLetlow.com](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=bc26b475c0&e=95355a072c).

| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn’t a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal — the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God’s grace.**

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**“God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”**_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbhl8y&__onlt=h)
---

Charlie’s hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

...and it’s not just the conservative message as a whole — _**it’s the message of FAITH!**_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie’s call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it’s happening._

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we’re witnessing is not just growth —**it’s revival.**

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America’s faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up.**

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _“We’re not backing down.”_

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie’s most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie’s faith._**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

name: Pennsylvania Forward Party

body:
Candidates recruitment continues!

|
## Independence is our Future
Across the country, more voters are stepping away from the traditional 2 party system. Pennsylvania is no exception—recent reporting shows a surge in voters choosing to register as independents or with third parties. Read more on this below: [Lancaster Online 2/9- Number of independent and 3rd-party voters surges in Pa., despite being locked out of primaries](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=vYJyX3MbOxtbAs5yNTvbCCB3ByiMzo5EADpubumTvj-P17J8msmW8LZB_rXJF7AaHSZbUsn1LNFCbVABDdvYnTA9rJFe1mMd5B1v9hlsY9bzKHRvMGALBgZFzQEXDbnuga84jiGluvw6P4u-Y45HOYf47i17LGWI4fKopHMz4-YuU0QjbLoYdo8c5kMulI-wrjPOquMesQLILZZMqF0tD_e2tuPv6BPi83AvqB_Klm0&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=1) [Politics PA 10/28- Fun With Maps: PA Voter Registration by County (Oct 2025)](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=wWw1LGKe09YoyrHaTkDQ4FkZDgmSG69y1BFPH8YZhd6-sqYLBMcpQ9Xoz7guOYEAjA57CD397sB8TEtSJZ576oaX8rof8tWMq7XlWOIrLhHNBuPiG_uaYll3c867bkEN&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=2) [The Dallas Post 3/4- Luzerne County’s greatest voter registration growth isn’t Democrat or Republican](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=2Did5O5cbavH96nMuHbtvYwKleXnJYHxCMfO25OxlIOzSp1NVwSYy-6uLjNffk6nH4weP53LXmYtaueVuAen5nTKGeG0zDPIxnoLgxnp1F2HnmF2tI9xaFZjezWSyih6zzUkfTw6DcUi0Azd77uuPVSYAvyR37TKDA3GRQeFwjw&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=3) Our politics have gotten so toxic that people no longer want to be forced to choose a side. We're sick of everyone sticking with their team above all else thus dividing society in half. Americans know what to do when they only have bad options: **demand new options**. This scenario has played out over and over in our society. Whether it's in the cars we drive, food we eat, or entertainment we consume, old models of industry can't last when the consumers are unhappy. **The consumers of the politics industry are more than unhappy, they're furious.** **(Click below for our Candidate Recruitment Outline)**
## [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=MtBLw57MCBnd28lIl741u2f82VcN49yJ3Wou-X6QZ0hCrtoxosErjJZ-WOhV7ZNg-GRO_z0YjnCrE2d313L6Cw&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=4)
The change is already happening. Increasing numbers of candidates are choosing to run outside of the traditional parties. Sitting office holders are leaving their parties to be independent, see [this recent article about Lehigh County Commissioner Ron](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=tJRYktsaet6FBRlsPH718W939rbN-2cK70umxftCX4DqjPfQHqFOduDAOIhrCH0tn_5IRRypydTkk-jJlH6hTrG8Cdartc25vAYKOHfPtcQdAUO3342ezOoYOZjnslj8&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=5)[ Beitler](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=tJRYktsaet6FBRlsPH718W939rbN-2cK70umxftCX4DqjPfQHqFOduDAOIhrCH0tn_5IRRypydTkk-jJlH6hTrG8Cdartc25vAYKOHfPtcQdAUO3342ezOoYOZjnslj8&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=6) who left his party to serve as an independent. Organizations like ours are attacking the problems of ballot access and candidate support from every possible angle. In 10 years, we'll look at this as the low point of political division and lack of options. There are great candidates interested in working with us this year. The kinds of candidates who believe in a new kind of politics where the values are more important than which team you're on. We're Pennsylvanians who believe in a new kind of party. A party built by regular people, built from the ground up, one local race at a time. A party interested in supporting first time office seekers running in the 70% of races that otherwise, go uncontested. A party where people understand that the structure of our elections cannot let the parties control who gets on our ballots. The toxic politics of 2026 is dependent on there only being 2 options, which is why Americans are going to leave dependence in the past.
* * *
### Special Election Update
Last Month, there were two special elections to fill seats in the PA State House (Districts 22 and 42). They both were won by the Democrats. On 3/17, there will be two more(Districts 79 and 193). We will be reaching out to Forwardists in those areas to research and most importantly vote in these races. The Fifth special election now has a date, May 19th, also known as Primary Day! [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=lRFe1ojb2I3keveG6F1SNMpqnyA5DC-f4K2CG-ffZH4&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=7) On [January's statewide call](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=c1vIqT8LaeJ1yAWpG61iLl6fQsq-0_vrqRWgviHRXbWlMZEVxl0MBTeRVtDkSuMbFF0LNKsSEAr_F4dfjE1u3w&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_march_newsletter&n=8), we heard from recently-announced Forward affiliate Ron Ruman. He told us about his plan to run as a Forward Democrat for the PA State House in the 196th district (York County). On January 29th, Seth Grove announced his resignation, triggering this special election. Pennsylvania's antiquated closed primary system is particularly relevant in this situation. Ron is relying on support from independent voters to win his race, but independents know they don't normally vote on primary day, so their turnout would naturally be low. **Ron needs help getting the word out to all the independents in his district that THIS ELECTION, they can indeed turnout to have their voice heard. clean_body: Candidates recruitment continues! | Independence is our Future Across the country, more voters are stepping away from the traditional 2 party system. Pennsylvania is no exception—recent reporting shows a surge in voters choosing to register as independents or with third parties. Read more on this below: Our politics have gotten so toxic that people no longer want to be forced to choose a side. We're sick of everyone sticking with their team above all else thus dividing society in half. Americans know what to do when they only have bad options: demand new options. This scenario has played out over and over in our society. Whether it's in the cars we drive, food we eat, or entertainment we consume, old models of industry can't last when the consumers are unhappy. The consumers of the politics industry are more than unhappy, they're furious. (Click below for our Candidate Recruitment Outline) The change is already happening. Increasing numbers of candidates are choosing to run outside of the traditional parties. Sitting office holders are leaving their parties to be independent, see who left his party to serve as an independent. Organizations like ours are attacking the problems of ballot access and candidate support from every possible angle. In 10 years, we'll look at this as the low point of political division and lack of options. There are great candidates interested in working with us this year. The kinds of candidates who believe in a new kind of politics where the values are more important than which team you're on. We're Pennsylvanians who believe in a new kind of party. A party built by regular people, built from the ground up, one local race at a time. A party interested in supporting first time office seekers running in the 70% of races that otherwise, go uncontested. A party where people understand that the structure of our elections cannot let the parties control who gets on our ballots. The toxic politics of 2026 is dependent on there only being 2 options, which is why Americans are going to leave dependence in the past. Special Election Update Last Month, there were two special elections to fill seats in the PA State House (Districts 22 and 42). They both were won by the Democrats. On 3/17, there will be two more(Districts 79 and 193). We will be reaching out to Forwardists in those areas to research and most importantly vote in these races. The Fifth special election now has a date, May 19th, also known as Primary Day! On , we heard from recently-announced Forward affiliate Ron Ruman. He told us about his plan to run as a Forward Democrat for the PA State House in the 196th district (York County). On January 29th, Seth Grove announced his resignation, triggering this special election. Pennsylvania's antiquated closed primary system is particularly relevant in this situation. Ron is relying on support from independent voters to win his race, but independents know they don't normally vote on primary day, so their turnout would naturally be low. Ron needs help getting the word out to all the independents in his district that THIS ELECTION, they can indeed turnout to have their voice heard. Please reach out if you're interested in helping. Join us for our monthly call. It's the best way to follow all the things happening with the PA Forward Party. Also remember to join your regional calls to work with others near you. # [Thanks to Donald Trump, the ultra-wealthy are getting ahead](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=189897645&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg5ODk3NjQ1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzI4MTY0NjUsImV4cCI6MTc3NTQwODQ2NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.iRT71rQEIL1WQy9tIi1uFlWIN3IJZ0pIDZza7armzI0)
### Michigan's working families are getting left behind.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Mar 6
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..n3qpSEYzV4d6ffG7vBFUua4oQmblrMvUwfizbnkHoa4?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/thanks-to-donald-trump-the-ultra?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

I've been thinking a lot about fairness lately.
When I meet Michiganders on the campaign trail, I find myself thinking:
_How can I fight for these folks? How can I make sure they 're heard?_
**Because more and more, it feels like there are two sets of rules:**
**One for the powerful. And one for everyone else.**
If you're a billionaire in Donald Trump's America? Things are going great. Wealth buys access. It buys influence. It can even buy you a pardon if you need one.
But if you're a working family here in Michigan? It's very different.
This has been on my mind because in our Senate race, a Texas oil billionaire named Tim Dunn poured $5 million into a super PAC backing my Republican opponent.
**Five. Million. Dollars.**
That's an unfathomable amount of money. And it's being spent to try to influence _our_ race.
Here's what really bothers me: Tim Dunn doesn't care about Michigan.
He just sees Michigan as a political investment opportunity. A chance to buy power.
And he's been very clear about his worldview. He has openly said he believes only certain Christians should hold leadership positions in government. And he's using his wealth to try to shape our country accordingly.
I'm sorry, but that's not how it works in America. It can't be.
But here's the bigger issue: This isn't just about one megadonor or one campaign.
**It 's about an administration that's tilting things more and more toward the people who already have the most.**
That's why billionaires get tax breaks while working families struggle to afford health insurance. It's why Trump's friends are protected while everyone else is told to play by the rules.
We're told there's no money for schools, no money for rural health clinics, no money for infrastructure - but somehow there's always money for another favor for the people at the top.
That doesn't happen by accident.
I'll be honest - when you see $5 million in MAGA billionaire money drop into your state overnight, it can feel overwhelming. But then I think about why I fight so hard for Michigan in the first place.
I grew up here in Michigan. I love it here. My parents ran a small business here. My dad was a Detroit public school teacher. I've been working since I was young - and I've spent my career fighting for Michigan workers.
I've sat at tables across this state - in union halls, in diners, at community colleges - listening to Michiganders who work hard, play by the rules, and still feel like they're falling behind.
Here's the thing: These folks aren't asking for yachts. They're asking for fairness. They want a government that works for working people, not just Trump's wealthy and well-connected friends.
**Look, I 'm the only candidate in this race who isn't a millionaire. **And I don't say that as a talking point. I say it because it shapes how I see this moment.
I know what it's like to budget carefully. I know what it's like to worry about the grocery bill. I pay my rent every month like so many of you.
When MAGA megadonors try to buy influence here, I take it personally.
Not because it's about me, but because of what it says about how they see Michigan.
Michigan is a state of manufacturers. Of autoworkers. Of teachers. Of nurses. Of small-business owners. Of families who show up, do the work, and look out for each other.
I'm sorry, but we don't take orders from MAGA billionaires from Texas.
If we hold our lead in the polls and win this race, it won't be because of one massive check.
**[It will be because thousands of people chipped in what they could because they believe this Michigan Senate seat belongs to Michigan voters.](https://substack.com/redirect/95eccf22-3c7d-4667-9f67-93e2a76bdbff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Chip In Now](https://substack.com/redirect/95eccf22-3c7d-4667-9f67-93e2a76bdbff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you're able to contribute to our grassroots campaign, I'd be grateful. Truly. Regular folks taking action together is how we compete with this kind of money from megadonors.
But more than anything, I'm grateful you're here.
This is bigger than one race. It's about whether we accept that there are two sets of rules, or we fight back.
For me, fairness is still worth fighting for. Michigan is worth fighting for.
More soon.
With grit,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

Thousands of folks have already made a donation — and now, they’re counting on you to do the same.
#

Hi, it’s Gabby. I wanted to share this message from my friend Sherrod Brown. Sherrod is a gun safety champion who is running for the US Senate in Ohio. I hope you’ll take a minute to read his message below, then chip in anything you can. Thank you. -GG

* * *

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-brown-2026.VLItMQ&refcode=em260306-1-b&t=1&akid=11297%2E3935704%2EKX7AWP)

$10.
That’s how much I’m asking you to chip in today — split between my campaign and GIFFORDS — to help us reach our $25,000 goal and win in Ohio. [**Can we count on you?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giffords-em-brown-2026.bbh7ad&refcode=em260306-1-b&t=2&akid=11297%2E3935704%2EKX7AWP)

If you knew that by giving $10 now, you could guarantee we flip this Senate seat and defeat my opponent, wouldn’t you donate immediately?
If you knew that by giving $10 now, you could help us fight back against misleading attack ads and reach more voters with the truth, wouldn’t you chip in?

But by the time you get to this point in the email, thousands of folks have already given their $10 — and now, they’re counting on you to do the same.
With a new poll showing me 1 point ahead of my opponent, we can flip this seat — but not unless we capitalize on our momentum and hit our critical grassroots fundraising goals.

disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Citizens to Elect Rick Larsen
body:
Families in Northwest Washington want lower prices and less war from this Administration.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126796620/605980162/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZTI0M2M1Zi03ZjE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QDWrYpQyvGY5omMnoS7qph58A2Fl1-vn1qIW8gxC7Z4=&emci=7acfea1a-e218-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=2e243c5f-7f19-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=9494239)
---

| | Yesterday, I voted against President Trump's reckless war, which he has not justified to the American people or Congress. **Families in Northwest Washington want lower prices and less war from this Administration, but they are getting higher prices and more war.** No one is lamenting the fate of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. The President, however, has provided no clear objectives or plan for the ongoing combat operations against Iran, which have already cost six American servicemembers their lives. As I have done in the past and will continue to do, I honor and respect the women and men of the United States military. My thoughts are with the families of the six women and men killed in this conflict. Yesterday, I voted yes on a resolution that directs President Trump to remove the U.S. military from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran and its military, unless such hostilities are explicitly authorized by Congress. The resolution failed by a final vote of 212 to 219. Even with the loss of this resolution, I will continue to hold this administration accountable and make sure they hear the truth. **Americans want lower prices, not more war.** More soon, _Rick_ |

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: I am against supplemental funding for the illegal Iran war.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Last year Trump and the GOP told us our financial outlook as a nation was in such dire straits that they HAD to pass $1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid.
#

I think it’s important to be clear on this:
I am not going to vote to spend any more of the American taxpayer’s money on an illegal war with Iran.
Last year Trump and the GOP told us our financial outlook was in such dire straits that they HAD to pass $1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid. We couldn’t possibly afford extending the subsidies keeping health care affordable for millions of people. They cut the VA, USAID, education, housing, medical research, even the National Weather Service — and that’s not even half of it.
Now they want $1 billion a day and MORE for this war that no one wants, that they haven’t justified, that they are waging illegally and without Congressional authorization.
Congress appropriated close to a trillion dollars for the Department of Defense last year, and Trump is asking for a full trillion dollars this year. So, no, I’m not voting to fund this war. They can check the seat cushions if they have to.
We can’t let up. We need to remind Trump and the GOP that we do not want this war, and we have to do it every single day.
[**If you are with me against this war, add your name here to make that 100% crystal clear.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260306-IRAN-EM/?refcode=em260306-1-120&akid=4087%2E734936%2EcL0hOX)
[SIGN ON](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260306-IRAN-EM/?source=em260306-1-120&akid=4087%2E734936%2EcL0hOX)
Thank you.
Ruben

I’m officially the Democratic nominee for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat, and I’m running against Republican Michael Whatley, a far-right lobbyist and President Trump’s handpicked candidate.
| | | | | [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6765?t=6&akid=704%2E124072%2EQEjN2z)
---
Peter, it’s official!

Earlier this week, I won the Democratic nomination for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat. I’ll be running against Republican Michael Whatley, a far-right Big Oil lobbyist and President Trump’s handpicked candidate.
As I start my general election campaign, I’m thinking about how grateful I am for the support of folks like you that got me here. **This is the time to stand up and fight for our future – and I am ready. But I need you with me.**
**[My team and I have set a goal to raise $100,000 before tonight at midnight to kick off the general election campaign. Will you chip in $5 today to help us win the biggest Senate race in the country, break the GOP’s hold on Washington and return power to the people?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6765?t=7&akid=704%2E124072%2EQEjN2z)**

I didn’t plan to run for federal office. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home. But when I look at what’s happening across the country, I know I can’t leave things as they are for my daughters or for yours.
So long as Trump’s extreme allies are in power, there is no path to accountability or restraint. Just more chaos, division and attacks on our fundamental freedoms.
**To set our nation back on course, we must regain Senate control – and that starts by winning in North Carolina.** We can flip this seat from red to blue for the first time since 2008, but far-right Republican PACs and megadonors will spend hundreds of millions to stop us.
**[Whether they succeed depends on people like you, Peter, stepping up to help us hit our goal before tonight. Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us reach our fundraising goal and build the momentum we need to win?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6765?t=12&akid=704%2E124072%2EQEjN2z)**
Thank you for everything.

Roy

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.
