From higher health insurance premium costs, to massive cuts to Medicaid, Texans of all walks of life are feeling the negative impacts. Healthcare is a human right at TOP , and at this critical time with our healthcare system looking bleak, we want to hear from YOU – members, supporters, and community allies. Weigh in on what REAL healthcare looks like to you, and share your personal story. [] GIVE US A BOOST: Help TOP host a panel at this year's Netroots Nation conference [] TOP applied to host a panel at Netroots Nation this year, and we'd love your VOTE to make this panel a reality. It'll take you less than a minute to show your support, and it'll get us closer to sharing TOP's theory of change on the national stage with hundreds of progressive activists and organizers from across the country. Just follow these quick steps: 1. Check out our panel topic, "Texas: MAGA before MAGA and how we can still win!" [] 2. Click on the blue "Vote for this submission" button. 3. Create a new account if you need to, or log in to your existing Netroots account. 4. Select our panel and vote! Feel free to share the panel link on your social media, and use the hashtag #NN26 . TRUMP TRACKER: The FIFA Peace Prize winner sure likes war [] Welcome to another edition of our Trump Tracker, where we apply Critical Ignoring [] to help fight the right-wing's "flood the zone" [] approach that seeks to divide and demoralize us. No matter how the White House tries to spin it, the truth is that Donald Trump is entrenching the U.S. in another completely unnecessary war (this horrendous administration can't justify it), all to distract from his sinking poll numbers, scandals, and domestic policy failures. [] And Republicans on Capitol Hill are too cowardly to stop him. On top of the violence being inflicted on civilians, this foreign policy aggression from our self-declared "Peace President" has already cost U.S. taxpayers more than $5 billion in only a few days of operations — funds that could cover SNAP benefits for more than 2 million people in the U.S.! [] To make matters worse, POTUS and his MAGA loyalists couldn't care less about the estimated hundreds of thousands of lives they are displacing through this military escalation. [] So what's the foreign policy of Trump 2.0? Staight-up imperialism. [] Español TERMINANDO CON UNA NOTA ALTA: Mostrando la fuerza de nuestras comunidades en estas elecciones primarias [] ¡Eso es todo! En medio de una votación récord en todo el estado, el equipo de TOP PAC para impulsar el voto se hizo sentir, conectando y movilizando a 109,000 votantes texanos para que emitieran su voto por una lista de líderes progresistas respaldados. ¡Esto es poder popular y poder político en acción! TOP se fundó con la convicción de que nuestras comunidades negras y latinas, a menudo ignoradas por quienes ostentan el poder, merecen una voz, no solo un lugar en la mesa. Durante más de 15 años, hemos sumado a miles de tejanos al movimiento, respaldando a líderes e impulsando políticas que buscan mejorar la vida cotidiana: líderes probadas y sin complejos como Jasmine Crockett y Gina Hinojosa , quienes han demostrado su compromiso con la defensa de nuestras comunidades. Y aunque no todas las contiendas electorales resultaron como esperábamos en estas primarias, nuestra labor de acercamiento a los votantes ayudó a 12 de nuestros 15 candidatos respaldados a conseguir victorias o llegar a la segunda vuelta. El futuro de Texas se forjará con conversaciones importantes: las que mantenemos en los vecindarios mediante la organización y nuestro trabajo para promover el voto. Ahora más que nunca, ante el aumento de los esfuerzos de la extrema derecha por difundir desinformación, sembrar el miedo y restringir el acceso al voto (como lo que vimos en el condado de Dallas el día de las elecciones), nuestro trabajo es esencial. Mientras tanto, seguiremos involucrando a nuestras comunidades negras y latinas en torno a una visión audaz de seguridad y prosperidad compartidas que priorice a nuestras comunidades. ¡Manos a la obra! ¡Nos vemos en la segunda vuelta! RESPONDA NUESTRA ENCUESTA: Opine sobre cómo la atención médica le impacta [] Los ataques al acceso y la asequibilidad de la atención médica bajo la administración Trump 2.0 no han sido ninguna broma. Desde el aumento de las primas de los seguros médicos hasta los recortes masivos a Medicaid, los tejanos de todos los ámbitos están sintiendo los impactos negativos. La atención médica es un derecho humano en TOP , y en este momento crítico con nuestro sistema de salud en declive, queremos saber de USTEDES: miembros, simpatizantes y aliados de la comunidad. Opine sobre cómo ve la atención médica REAL y comparta su historia personal. [] VOTA POR NOSOTROS: Ayuda a TOP a organizar un panel en la conferencia Netroots Nation de este año [] TOP solicitó organizar un panel en Netroots Nation este año, y nos encantaría contar con su VOTO para hacerlo realidad. Le tomará menos de un minuto mostrar su apoyo , y nos ayudará a acercarnos a compartir la teoría de cambio de TOP en el escenario nacional con cientos de activistas y organizadores progresistas de todo el país. Solo sigue estos pasos: 1. Consulta el tema de nuestro panel: "Texas: ¡MAGA antes de MAGA y cómo aún podemos ganar!" [] 2. Haz clic en el botón azul "Vota por esta propuesta." 3. Crea una cuenta nueva si lo necesitas o inicia sesión en tu cuenta de Netroots. 4. ¡Selecciona nuestro panel y vota! Comparte el enlace del panel en tus redes sociales y usa la etiqueta #NN26 . RASTREADOR DE TRUMP: El ganador del Premio de la Paz de la FIFA realmente disfruta de la guerra [] Bienvenidos a otra edición de nuestro Rastreador de Trump , donde aplicamos la Ignorancia Crítica [] para ayudar a combatir el enfoque de la derecha de "inundar la zona" [] que busca dividirnos y desmoralizarnos. No importa cómo la Casa Blanca intente presentarlo, la verdad es que Donald Trump está atrincherando a Estados Unidos en otra guerra completamente innecesaria (esta horrenda administración no puede justificarla), todo para distraer la atención de sus desplomes en las encuestas, escándalos y fracasos en la política interna. [] Y los republicanos en el Capitolio son demasiado cobardes para detenerlo. Además de la violencia que se inflige a la población civil, esta agresión en política exterior por parte de nuestro autoproclamado "Presidente de la Paz" ya ha costado a los contribuyentes estadounidenses más de 5 mil millones de dólares en tan solo unos días de operaciones: ¡fondos que podrían cubrir las prestaciones del SNAP para más de 2 millones de personas en Estados Unidos! [] Para empeorar las cosas, al presidente de Estados Unidos y a sus partidarios de MAGA les importan un bledo los cientos de miles de vidas que se estima que están desplazando con esta escalada militar. Entonces, ¿cuál es la política exterior de Trump 2.0? Imperialismo. [] Copyright (C) 2026 Texas Organizing Project. All rights reserved. Texas Organizing Project P.O. body:
Colorado is strongest when we're fighting together.

I wanted to share this photo with you: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126808572/606019476/1664162816?refcode=email_030626_throwbackphoto&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGRkNGEyMi05NzE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lGAHerZR5rbpxLYr_otR3Qa4p534JuQgPhhkHiTD-_U=) That’s me in front of the Wynkoop in downtown Denver (before I experienced the miracle of LASIK). After the company where I worked as a geologist was sold, the entire staff — including me — was laid off. I didn’t want a boss. I turned this idea of Colorado’s first brewpub, in an abandoned warehouse district, into a rough-and-ready small business. When I was running the Wynkoop, I was frustrated by the cut-throat culture of the restaurant industry. We started promoting our competition, telling the staff that our real competition was the TV set, and our job was to get people off the couch, out the door, and to enjoy life with their friends and family. I saw the same thing in local politics — it was all about winning, and then governing by making decisions mostly based on how to win the next election. **So I ran for public office to change that. Every day since, I've worked to bring folks together, improve each other’s ideas, and to actually get things done for Colorado.** In the Senate, we’ve worked with activists, businesses, and NGO’s to prioritize America’s most pressing needs. Together, we’ve invested billions in American manufacturing, created good-paying jobs, cut drug prices for seniors, and made the largest investment to tackle climate change in our country’s history. But President Trump has made it very clear that he doesn’t share our same commitment to bringing people together. He wants all power centered on himself and a small circle in the White House. Trump has worked to overwhelm and divide us. He’s ripped away health care funding, denied disaster relief funding to Coloradans recovering from wildfires and flooding, and threatened our state’s child care funding. He vetoed our bipartisan bill that would bring clean water to 50,000 rural Coloradans. **Take it from me: From a small business in Denver to the U.S. Senate, I’ve seen firsthand that Colorado is strongest when we’re united in fighting together.** **_[Right now, we're standing together to protect child care and health care, demand disaster relief funding, push back against Trump’s mob boss tactics, and get sh*t done for Colorado — and we hope you’ll stand with us. clean_body: Colorado is strongest when we're fighting together. I wanted to share this photo with you: = That’s me in front of the Wynkoop in downtown Denver (before I experienced the miracle of LASIK). After the company where I worked as a geologist was sold, the entire staff — including me — was laid off. I didn’t want a boss. I turned this idea of Colorado’s first brewpub, in an abandoned warehouse district, into a rough-and-ready small business. When I was running the Wynkoop, I was frustrated by the cut-throat culture of the restaurant industry. We started promoting our competition, telling the staff that our real competition was the TV set, and our job was to get people off the couch, out the door, and to enjoy life with their friends and family. I saw the same thing in local politics — it was all about winning, and then governing by making decisions mostly based on how to win the next election. So I ran for public office to change that. Every day since, I've worked to bring folks together, improve each other’s ideas, and to actually get things done for Colorado. In the Senate, we’ve worked with activists, businesses, and NGO’s to prioritize America’s most pressing needs. Together, we’ve invested billions in American manufacturing, created good-paying jobs, cut drug prices for seniors, and made the largest investment to tackle climate change in our country’s history. But President Trump has made it very clear that he doesn’t share our same commitment to bringing people together. He wants all power centered on himself and a small circle in the White House. Trump has worked to overwhelm and divide us. He’s ripped away health care funding, denied disaster relief funding to Coloradans recovering from wildfires and flooding, and threatened our state’s child care funding. He vetoed our bipartisan bill that would bring clean water to 50,000 rural Coloradans. Take it from me: From a small business in Denver to the U.S. Senate, I’ve seen firsthand that Colorado is strongest when we’re united in fighting together. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | = | = | | | = | = | | | = | = Thanks for standing with us, John | | Email is a key way for us to stay in touch and make sure you get the latest updates from our campaign. This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Special operator and private military contractor with over 15 deployments who now leads rescue operations, humanitarian and medical aid – all led by the Holy Spirit “to free the oppressed, so others may live.” **Since 2022, I've been the founder and leader of Heroes for Humanity – a network of special operators, veterans, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday people committed to being the hands and feet of Jesus.** We were born in the chaos of Afghanistan's fall in 2021 – where I personally helped evacuate 77 Americans and vetted Afghan allies, even swimming the Panjshir River behind enemy lines to pull people out. And just the other day, we rescued 8 families from the chaos and violence in Mexico. But our story goes much deeper than even that.
---
---

Rules are rules...or they're nothing Peter, one of the ways I put myself through college was working as a youth sports referee.

_I've had coaches yell at me.

I've had parents lose their minds in the bleachers.

And I've had players do everything they could to try to change the call._

But here's the thing: despite the noise, I always knew that when the ref blows the whistle and makes the call — that's it. **You don't get to ignore it just because you don't like it. That's how the game works.**

**The Supreme Court made a call on Trump's tariffs by calling them unconstitutional. He didn't like it...so he doubled down anyway. And instead of making sure he plays fair, Republicans in Congress are standing there like it's no big deal and doing absolutely nothing.**

_But it IS a big deal, Peter._

If the referee doesn't matter, the rules don't matter. And if the rules don't matter, we don't have a system in place to ensure things are ordered and fair. Instead, all we have is chaos. I didn't tolerate players or bystanders ignoring the whistle back then, and we shouldn't tolerate it now. That's why taking back the House — and restoring real accountability — matters so much right now.

clean_body: Rules are rules...or they're nothing Peter, one of the ways I put myself through college was working as a youth sports referee. I've had coaches yell at me. I've had parents lose their minds in the bleachers. And I've had players do everything they could to try to change the call. But here's the thing: despite the noise, I always knew that when the ref blows the whistle and makes the call — that's it. You don't get to ignore it just because you don't like it. That's how the game works. The Supreme Court made a call on Trump's tariffs by calling them unconstitutional. He didn't like it...so he doubled down anyway. And instead of making sure he plays fair, Republicans in Congress are standing there like it's no big deal and doing absolutely nothing. But it IS a big deal, Peter. If the referee doesn't matter, the rules don't matter. And if the rules don't matter, we don't have a system in place to ensure things are ordered and fair. Instead, all we have is chaos. I didn't tolerate players or bystanders ignoring the whistle back then, and we shouldn't tolerate it now. name: David Hogg
subject: Democratic voters are fed up, and so are we
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
The Democratic Party is painfully out of touch and choosing caution over conviction — voters are tired of it.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260306-1&t=1&akid=3220%2E587540%2EeBT7Xh)
Peter,
The biggest issue facing our party right now is the growing gap between voters and leadership. The Democratic Party has been painfully out of touch for a while now, and voters are done pretending otherwise.
You don’t have to take our word for it. Voters told The New York Times exactly how they feel:
[ ](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260306_1_focus.NAYbra&refcode=em20260306-3220&t=2&akid=3220%2E587540%2EeBT7Xh)
[ ](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260306_1_focus.NAYbra&refcode=em20260306-3220&t=3&akid=3220%2E587540%2EeBT7Xh)
These are not words used to describe a party that inspires people or lasting change. This is what voters say when they’ve been let down again and again.
**Democrats have left their constituents feeling abandoned, unheard, and fed up with a party that talks more than it delivers.**
Even more than that, **Democrats have a courage problem.** Too many of them won’t stand up and address the issues facing working people because they’re too busy worrying about what their donors will say.
And the result? Leadership that is insulated from our frustration and disconnected from the very people they’re supposed to represent.
But the good news is, these voters have also been clear about what they want to see instead:
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260306_1_focus.NAYbra&refcode=em20260306-3220&t=4&akid=3220%2E587540%2EeBT7Xh)
There’s _nothing_ subtle about that.
Voters see what’s happening within the Democratic Party, and they’re tired of it. They want bold, new progressive leadership who will speak plainly about what’s at stake, and fight for working people without flinching.
Because while ICE is ripping families apart, Trump is starting more forever wars, costs are skyrocketing, and the reality of homeownership is drifting farther and farther out of reach for young people, **too many Democrats are choosing caution over conviction.**
That’s why Leaders We Deserve exists. We aren’t interested in keeping the same tired playbook alive that has left the Democratic Party stagnant for so long. We’re doing the work to elect bold, young progressives who will truly put up a fight for their constituents and deliver on the issues that matter to them most.
And our slate of candidates isn’t compromised by corporate cash or billionaire donors, because their campaigns are powered by grassroots supporters like you. That means it’s _your_ voice that’s shaping their political agendas, not lobbyists or special interests.
**[So Peter, if you believe in our power to transform the Democratic Party and put real leaders in office to fight for working people, will you pitch in $5 today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260306_1_focus.NAYbra&refcode=em20260306-3220&amount=5&t=5&akid=3220%2E587540%2EeBT7Xh)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260306_1_focus.NAYbra&amount=5&refcode=em20260306-3220&t=24&akid=3220%2E587540%2EeBT7Xh)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

Here’s the thing: In a state as competitive as Pennsylvania, no candidate can win by preaching to the choir. You have to reach out to independent voters and folks who, frankly, won’t agree with everything you have to say.
But Derek, that’s why I ran for Governor in the first place. Pennsylvania is a big state — and yes, we have our fair share of differences. But I also know this:
**There is so much more that unites us as Pennsylvanians than what divides us.**
Talk to any of your neighbors, Republican or Democrat. And what you’ll hear from nearly every Pennsylvanian? They all want the same things. They all want to send their kids to good schools. They want to bring down the cost of living and make life more affordable. They want to live their lives how we see fit, without the government standing in the way.
That’s what this campaign is all about, Derek — and I really believe it’s a winning message. But the only way we can get that message out to all 67 counties across Pennsylvania? We need to build a historic campaign — with historic investment to reach Democrats, Republicans, and independents alike.
[_**If we want to win these voters over, we can’t just reach them once. We need to reach them again and again, from now until the moment polls close on Election Day — and that takes a lot of resources. So please: Can you chip in whatever you can and make sure we avoid any budget cuts at tomorrow’s finance meeting?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126810119/606024149/1751931448?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&refcode=email_030626_alone&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZGUxNzc3OC05YzE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8JBO6NbdZW1ZV181UYkfVLGg14jQsl0ahxO9OOmIewU=)

body:
Peter,

The Supreme Court made it clear: Trump's tariffs were illegal.

That should have been a moment for the president to step back, listen to the law, and put American families first.

But, of course, that's not what happened.

Trump reacted by trying to find a workaround for the Supreme Court decision, and announced a new 15% global tariff anyway. In his own words, he plans to go further, not back down — even after the highest court said he doesn’t have that power.

**In 2025 alone, the average household spent about $1,000 more because of Trump's tariffs.** That's $1,000 that could have gone to groceries, rent, school supplies, medical bills, or saving for the future. These are real costs that hardworking families are suffering through.

These Trump tariffs have meant extra stress, tighter budgets, and impossible choices. They've harmed small businesses and entire industries, and have done permanent damage to American farmers.

Our country needs leaders who take public service seriously, who understand that the Oval Office is not a personal playground but a place to serve the American people. For decades, the Supreme Court operated quietly. Big cases followed a
timeline. Justices were assumed impartial. Most Americans didn’t need to
watch daily.

Those days are gone.

Top Supreme Court reporters recently laid it all out: the Court is now
polarized and secretive. Ethics rules are toothless. Schedules are opaque.
The public has almost no insight into who influences what decisions.

One reporter said the Court’s “default secrecy... increases suspicion.”
Another noted it took years to adopt a weak ethics code. A third
highlighted that rulings like Trump’s broad immunity decisions were
produced with almost no transparency.

This is a captured court at work.

Trump’s appointments have created a 6–3 conservative supermajority that is
now helping rubber-stamp his agenda, allowing misuse of the shadow docket,
and enabling his extremism.

And the scariest part? The Court is now stepping in where Congress has
failed — amplifying its own power while Americans watch from the
sidelines.

The reporters made it clear: this is a court detached from the public, yet
controlling almost every aspect of our rights — from voting to women’s
healthcare to immigration. We cannot let a secretive, partisan, and
ethically fragile court dictate the future of our country.

We’re fighting back. We’re exposing corruption, pushing for reform, and
defending a judiciary that answers to the people — not political
operatives. But we cannot do it alone.

body:

| | Peter,

The Trump Administration is operating as if they are above the law, and the consequences in our communities have been devastating.

For years, we’ve watched ICE operate with a lack of transparency and a surplus of aggression. But under this administration, the situation has reached a breaking point. We are seeing a militarized force invading our neighborhoods with almost no restraint, chasing arrest quotas instead of focusing on genuine threats.

Ousting DHS Secretary Kristi Noem isn’t enough to solve the problem – it’s no guarantee of any changes to ICE’s conduct, certainly not if she’s replaced with another extreme MAGA loyalist.

[I am not backing down. We must keep up the public pressure and continue demanding accountability and reform. If you’re with me, add your name here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811577/606029507/2022988464?refcode2=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&refcode=SP_EM_PT_90DO_260306_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzY3OTc3ZS1hMDE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htue_ttNehjPoCkRX9k5iPVp1xiqU32Ssk2ZFmKYRgk=&emci=0b67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=5258741)

Last year, I introduced the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act to finally rein in these reckless tactics. **This isn't just a policy debate, it's about basic human rights and public safety.**

My bill would:
* **Restrict military-style equipment** like tear gas and flash-bang grenades.
* **Mandate body cameras** for all immigration enforcement actions.
* **Restrict the use of masks** so agents can no longer hide behind anonymity.
* **Require de-escalation training** and the duty to intervene when a colleague acts unlawfully.

[If you agree that no federal agency should have a "blank check" to terrorize our communities, will you add your voice now to help us keep the pressure on the Trump Administration?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811578/606029508/2022988464?refcode2=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&refcode=SP_EM_PT_90DO_260306_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzY3OTc3ZS1hMDE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htue_ttNehjPoCkRX9k5iPVp1xiqU32Ssk2ZFmKYRgk=&emci=0b67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=5258741) | | **[SIGN ON](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811579/606029509/2022988464?refcode2=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&refcode=SP_EM_PT_90DO_260306_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzY3OTc3ZS1hMDE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htue_ttNehjPoCkRX9k5iPVp1xiqU32Ssk2ZFmKYRgk=&emci=0b67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=5258741)**

The tragic deaths of U.S. citizens like Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti are proof of what happens when law enforcement is stripped of oversight. We cannot allow this conduct to be normalized.

I’ve already voted against further ICE funding because I refuse to give more money to an agency that refuses to reform. But I need you with me in this fight to ensure our message is heard loud and clear in Washington.

[Please, add your support today to help us demand the transparency and reform our country deserves.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811580/606029510/2022988464?refcode2=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&refcode=SP_EM_PT_90DO_260306_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzY3OTc3ZS1hMDE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htue_ttNehjPoCkRX9k5iPVp1xiqU32Ssk2ZFmKYRgk=&emci=0b67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=1c67977e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=5258741)

**Boysko Bulletin: Week Eight Report From Richmond**
---
Dear Peter, One of the most important jobs of the General Assembly is passing a balanced budget as required by the Virginia Constitution. Last week, the Senate finished work on its [budget amendments](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811604/606029621/-665051936?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjFmYTE1OWUtYTAxOS1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhMWYwYTk3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=7xcStLMG57ZqJJ7kBDGbUFHzmLbBgLZ_-6HMvsAS_oA=&emci=c913bef6-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=21fa159e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=22486556) and the House finished work on its [budget amendments](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811605/606029622/613044845?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjFmYTE1OWUtYTAxOS1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhMWYwYTk3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=7xcStLMG57ZqJJ7kBDGbUFHzmLbBgLZ_-6HMvsAS_oA=&emci=c913bef6-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=21fa159e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=22486556). Now the two Chambers are working to reconcile their separate floor approved budget amendments. We have also been debating and voting on legislation that passed the other Chamber. Our focus for budget decisions was on affordability. Our work was challenging as a result of the federal actions threatening Medicaid coverage and driving up health insurance costs. The Senate budget protects coverage, stabilizing the individual market, restoring access to healthcare, and strengthening public health, all without cutting core services or shifting the burden onto working families. This is a budget grounded in fairness and fiscal responsibility. The Senate budget raises wages, includes funding for my paid family and medical leave legislation, invests in opportunity, and ensures that industries benefiting from Virginia’s growth contribute to its future. This budget protects working families, strengthens public education and healthcare, invests in housing and transportation, and ensures powerful corporate interests contribute to the Commonwealth’s future. **Workforce and Wages: Higher Pay and Paid Leave for Working Virginians** The Senate advanced legislation, SB 1, to raise Virginia’s minimum wage to $15 per hour and my bill, SB 2, to create a paid family and medical leave insurance program. For thousands of Virginia families, this means financial stability during life’s most critical moments. SB 30 also invests directly in public workers:3% salary increases each year for state employees2% salary increases for state-supported local employees$560 million in workforce investment over the biennium$243 million in General Fund support for employee health insurance premiums **Food Access: Safeguarding SNAP & Expanding School Meals** In response to federal funding changes, SB 30 proactively protects food assistance programs:$135 million set aside in anticipation of SNAP cost-sharing requirements$100.4 million to address increased administrative cost shares$2 million for SNAP vendor support$2.4 million for a SNAP quality assurance team **Childcare: Expanding Access and Supporting Working Parents** The Senate establishes a $50 million biennial early childhood childcare pilot program that partners with employers and higher education institutions to expand access. This targeted investment directly addresses one of the largest affordability challenges facing Virginia families. **Affordable Housing: Investing in Affordable Communities** These investments promote mixed-income housing development while strengthening local economic infrastructure. SB 30 strengthens housing affordability through:$50 million in additional funding for the Virginia Housing Trust Fund$13 million for eviction prevention and diversion programsNearly $80 million redirected to provide grants directly to local governments for site development **Healthcare: Protecting Medicaid and Stabilizing Coverage** With potential federal Medicaid reductions and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, healthcare affordability faces significant uncertainty. SB 30 addresses a projected $3.2 billion Medicaid forecast challenge, without cutting eligibility or shifting costs onto working families. Healthcare investments include:Provides $200 million to offset the expiration of enhanced federal premium tax credits and stabilize the individual insurance marketEstablishes a $90 million Medicaid reserveRestores the FAMIS prenatal program$136.1 million for the Children’s Services Act$44.3 million to increase Medicaid personal care rates$22.5 million for developmental disability waiver rate increases$10 million for free clinic You can see the details of the House and Floor Approved Budget Amendments in The Commonwealth Institute’s [Key Budget Policy Choices](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811606/606029623/956070753?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjFmYTE1OWUtYTAxOS1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhMWYwYTk3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=7xcStLMG57ZqJJ7kBDGbUFHzmLbBgLZ_-6HMvsAS_oA=&emci=c913bef6-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=21fa159e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=22486556). I encourage you to vote for the Proposed Constitutional Amendment on Redistricting. A "yes" vote would allow the General Assembly to redraw Virginia's congressional districts, since other states have done so, in addition to giving effect to the proposed district map in time for the 2026 Congressional elections and return the responsibility of drawing the congressional districts in 2031 to the Virginia Redistricting Commission. A "no" vote would leave the authority to draw congressional districts with the Virginia Redistricting Commission once a decade and Virginia's current districts would remain in place. There is information on voting locations and hours below. We’ve completed eight weeks of the 2026 General Assembly Session with just one week more to go. The last couple of weeks have been very productive. Of the 19 of my bills that passed from the Senate to the House, 14 have passed the House and await the Governor’s signature, and 4 require further House action. I am thankful for each of you who have written to me and visited Richmond. See you back home soon! Kindest regards,

The bills have been sent to conference where [conferees ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811637/606029654/-1821246626?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjFmYTE1OWUtYTAxOS1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhMWYwYTk3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=7xcStLMG57ZqJJ7kBDGbUFHzmLbBgLZ_-6HMvsAS_oA=&emci=c913bef6-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=21fa159e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=22486556)will negotiate the differences and produce a final bill. The conference report will be voted on by the House and the Senate. Please reach out to your legislators asking them to vote against the casino bill. Alternatively, conditions can be added to the bill. The version of the bill passed by the House General Laws Committee included the following favorable provision: _Notwithstanding a vote in the affirmative by a majority of the voters of the locality in which the referendum was held, a referendum held pursuant to this section shall not be successful if a majority of the voters in the magisterial district in which the proposed casino gaming establishment is to be located do not vote in the affirmative._ As you know, the Hunter Mill and Dranesville districts remain opposed to a casino anywhere in Fairfax County, and especially in their communities. Unfortunately, that language was removed by the House Appropriations Committee. It is critical that the final conference language does not strip the locality of decision-making authority and force a referendum. [This past December the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors voted to oppose a casino in Tysons](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126811638/606029655/1657244779?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjFmYTE1OWUtYTAxOS1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhMWYwYTk3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=7xcStLMG57ZqJJ7kBDGbUFHzmLbBgLZ_-6HMvsAS_oA=&emci=c913bef6-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=21fa159e-a019-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=22486556).
This is not a partisan issue. The voters and residents of Fairfax county have overwhelmingly come out against this plan, and are deeply concerned about the ramifications of what a casino would mean. In every other case, casino proposals have been brought to the General Assembly at the specific request of the local government representing that community. For more than 70 years, The Arc of Virginia has been a driving force in advancing dignity, opportunity, and civil rights for individuals with disabilities across the Commonwealth. From challenging outdated systems to shaping forward-thinking public policy, this organization has led with courage, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to justice. But this work has never been solely about programs or services. It has always been about people — families advocating for their loved ones, self-advocates courageously sharing their lived experiences, leaders who understand the challenges firsthand, and allies who believe deeply in a Virginia where everyone belongs. No matter your background or how you connect to this mission, there is a place for you in this movement. In fact, your voice is essential. Together, we will continue building a more inclusive, more compassionate, and more just Virginia — where opportunity is not limited by ability, and where every person is valued. clean_body: | | | Boysko Bulletin: Week Eight Report From Richmond Dear Peter, One of the most important jobs of the General Assembly is passing a balanced budget as required by the Virginia Constitution. Last week, the Senate finished work on its and the House finished work on its . Now the two Chambers are working to reconcile their separate floor approved budget amendments. We have also been debating and voting on legislation that passed the other Chamber. Our focus for budget decisions was on affordability. Our work was challenging as a result of the federal actions threatening Medicaid coverage and driving up health insurance costs. The Senate budget protects coverage, stabilizing the individual market, restoring access to healthcare, and strengthening public health, all without cutting core services or shifting the burden onto working families. This is a budget grounded in fairness and fiscal responsibility. The Senate budget raises wages, includes funding for my paid family and medical leave legislation, invests in opportunity, and ensures that industries benefiting from Virginia’s growth contribute to its future. This budget protects working families, strengthens public education and healthcare, invests in housing and transportation, and ensures powerful corporate interests contribute to the Commonwealth’s future. Workforce and Wages: Higher Pay and Paid Leave for Working Virginians The Senate advanced legislation, SB 1, to raise Virginia’s minimum wage to $15 per hour and my bill, SB 2, to create a paid family and medical leave insurance program. For thousands of Virginia families, this means financial stability during life’s most critical moments. SB 30 also invests directly in public workers:3% salary increases each year for state employees2% salary increases for state-supported local employees$560 million in workforce investment over the biennium$243 million in General Fund support for employee health insurance premiums Food Access: Safeguarding SNAP & Expanding School Meals In response to federal funding changes, SB 30 proactively protects food assistance programs:$135 million set aside in anticipation of SNAP cost-sharing requirements$100.4 million to address increased administrative cost shares$2 million for SNAP vendor support$2.4 million for a SNAP quality assurance team Childcare: Expanding Access and Supporting Working Parents The Senate establishes a $50 million biennial early childhood childcare pilot program that partners with employers and higher education institutions to expand access. This targeted investment directly addresses one of the largest affordability challenges facing Virginia families. Affordable Housing: Investing in Affordable Communities These investments promote mixed-income housing development while strengthening local economic infrastructure. SB 30 strengthens housing affordability through:$50 million in additional funding for the Virginia Housing Trust Fund$13 million for eviction prevention and diversion programsNearly $80 million redirected to provide grants directly to local governments for site development Healthcare: Protecting Medicaid and Stabilizing Coverage With potential federal Medicaid reductions and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, healthcare affordability faces significant uncertainty. SB 30 addresses a projected $3.2 billion Medicaid forecast challenge, without cutting eligibility or shifting costs onto working families. Healthcare investments include:Provides $200 million to offset the expiration of enhanced federal premium tax credits and stabilize the individual insurance marketEstablishes a $90 million Medicaid reserveRestores the FAMIS prenatal program$136.1 million for the Children’s Services Act$44.3 million to increase Medicaid personal care rates$22.5 million for developmental disability waiver rate increases$10 million for free clinic You can see the details of the House and Floor Approved Budget Amendments in The Commonwealth Institute’s . I encourage you to vote for the Proposed Constitutional Amendment on Redistricting. A "yes" vote would allow the General Assembly to redraw Virginia's congressional districts, since other states have done so, in addition to giving effect to the proposed district map in time for the 2026 Congressional elections and return the responsibility of drawing the congressional districts in 2031 to the Virginia Redistricting Commission. A "no" vote would leave the authority to draw congressional districts with the Virginia Redistricting Commission once a decade and Virginia's current districts would remain in place. There is information on voting locations and hours below. We’ve completed eight weeks of the 2026 General Assembly Session with just one week more to go. The last couple of weeks have been very productive. Of the 19 of my bills that passed from the Senate to the House, 14 have passed the House and await the Governor’s signature, and 4 require further House action. I am thankful for each of you who have written to me and visited Richmond. See you back home soon! Kindest regards, Jennifer B. | | Houses in our neighborhoods should be homes for people, not a cash cow for hedge funds. Across the country, including right here in Oregon, hedge funds are wielding their financial muscle to gobble up available housing, outbid hard-working Americans who have sacrificed to save up downpayments, drive up home prices and rents, and turn neighborhoods into Wall Street profit centers at the expense of folks struggling to find a place to call home. **I've been fighting for years to push Wall Street out of the housing market, and I'm ready to work with anyone — Republican or Democrat — to get it done.** Here are three ways I'm taking concrete action to lower housing costs and expand homeownership: **First** , I've updated my HOPE for Homeownership Act and built bipartisan support behind it. This legislation would curb hedge funds' grip on our housing supply and ensure that homes in our communities are places for families to live — not assets for Wall Street speculation. **Second** , I'm partnering with Republican Senator Josh Hawley to address this crisis from an antitrust perspective. When a single corporate entity owns too much housing in a community, families lose real choices. Competition matters — especially when it comes to something as fundamental as a place to live. **Third** , I'm working with Senator Elizabeth Warren to end special tax breaks for the billionaire corporations buying up homes in our neighborhoods and reinvest those dollars into building more housing and lowering costs. Everyone should have a safe, affordable place to call home, and I'm working to get it done. name: Roy Cooper
subject: The hard work starts now.
body:
I’m officially the Democratic nominee for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat, and I’m running against Republican Michael Whatley, a far-right lobbyist and President Trump’s handpicked candidate.

| |
---
Friend, it’s official! Tuesday night, I won the Democratic nomination for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat. clean_body: No red tape should stand between our veterans and the complete federal benefits they've earned. As governor, I’ll fight to make sure the law reflects that. | | Hi Peter, Last week, Wisconsin veterans traveled to Washington, DC with a simple request: Let combat-injured veterans collect both their full VA disability benefits and the retirement pay they were promised. They came home empty-handed – because Ron Jonson blocked the bill that would have granted them their benefits. This is what it looks like when politicians say they "support the troops" but don't mean it. As governor, I’ll always fight for veterans to receive the benefits they’ve earned. Last week I met with the Portage County Dems Veterans Caucus, and shared my plans to take care of Wisconsin’s veterans. That means: Ensuring Title 32 and State Active Duty service counts toward federal VA eligibility Expanding property tax relief for disabled veterans to apply to veterans who are 70% disabled and more, rather than just 100% Supporting immediate VA healthcare access for all Guard members regardless of deployment length Fighting for simplified veteran status recognition so every Guard member who completes their service is federally recognized and receives the full benefits they have earned As governor, I will sign 100% property tax relief for disabled veterans the moment it hits my desk and fight every day to ensure our veterans get the benefits they’ve earned. Service is service. No red tape should stand between our veterans and the complete federal benefits they've earned. As governor, I’ll fight to make sure the law reflects that. Friend,
At last week’s State of the Union address, we heard the rumblings of a desperate man – of a failed President trying to cover his tracks. It was half lies, half grievances.
He tried to convince us that he hasn’t betrayed the American people with his cruel and chaotic agenda, but we are not falling for it.
Because we have witnessed Donald Trump unleash evil and brutality onto our streets. We have felt the squeeze as his pointless tariffs raise the costs of virtually everything. We have seen him sign the biggest cut to health care in U.S. history into law – all so his billionaire buddies can get a tax break.
**Today and every day, I’m using every tool at my disposal to push back against Donald Trump and the GOP’s dangerous agenda in the Senate. But to fight for you and your family as best as I can, it’s important that I hear from you directly about your top priorities and concerns.**
**[My team put together a new priorities survey so you can share your thoughts with me, and I’m counting on your response. Golden, Cuellar, Landsman, and Vargas. The vote came one day after the Senate killed a similar measure 47-53. Speaker Johnson called the resolution "dangerous" and said it would [empower enemies](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMHOpCAQhJ9Gb0yQdkAPHPbibfa6R9PTtCMJggF0sm-_YR_hv3Q6qUrVl_rzWl_og4-f33iwpduvLrm17lzwZqS6IXE5sBR_c-WyKqm0kCCkXmNYh95ZchpUz3YwRk0AMKl-tw7esG2bdmDQjASSJjLz2wDMYBip97YlSZBaDaN6zo8nSppnPQ4TsnZkulFep8PK5UEpFs43Vn-zjzG1L8UHpaMPdq_1LB386tTSqcWhD38JQ-Dc9E4traZTi4R2ns3CR6KMtYjM5_UOnjAWsaersKj5Ok7hM0bxxSzO9OVcOrX02brz60PwRTeyz4E-_AeoP9jstupfAAAA__-Wonvf). body:

#

Peter, With the Senate set to vote on the SAVE Act, I want to make sure that my position is heard loud and clear. **This bill is voter suppression — plain and simple.** The SAVE Act would force voters to produce hard-to-get citizenship documents just to vote — passports, perfectly matching birth certificates, or other documents many people don’t have easy access to. Their bill would keep women, people of color, rural voters, people with disabilities, and other eligible Americans from making their voices heard at the ballot box. This isn’t a fix for something that needs to be addressed. It’s a solution in search of a problem, and I refuse to support this roadblock that would keep millions of Americans from casting their ballots. [**Calling out voter suppression matters. [PETITION] [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126813848/606035845/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0ZjA2MDNjZi1hNTE5LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2ExZjBhOTciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Y42mEGHAqPRyY_K1tk2l9QgQZRmXAxu7u14LBTZeMAU=&emci=55220be1-9919-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=4f0603cf-a519-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=15820338)
---
Peter,

Like many of you, I'm watching the escalating conflict in the Middle East with a heavy heart. I'm praying for our troops, our allies, and the civilians caught in the middle of this violence.

Iran's government is a brutal dictatorship. It has committed serious human rights abuses and supported terrorism across the globe. The regime poses a real threat to our allies and to stability in the region, but that does **not** mean the president can take this country to war on his own.

That's why I voted yesterday to support a _War Powers_ resolution requiring the president to seek approval from Congress before taking further military action against Iran.**But Republicans voted it down.** Peter, our Constitution is clear: only Congress has the authority to declare war. If American servicemembers are going to be put in harm's way, the American people deserve a voice in that decision through their elected representatives.

Right now, _the Trump Administration owes the country answers._

If they truly have intelligence showing Iran is close to producing a nuclear weapon or an intercontinental ballistic missile, or poses an imminent threat to the United States, they must present that evidence and explain their strategy to Congress and the American people. War is too serious— _and the cost is too high_ —for anything less.

On Monday, Beto flew from El Paso to Houston to work with Powered by People volunteers at Texas Southern University. Afterwards he drove to Austin that night to meet volunteers the next morning at the University of Texas at Austin. The next day he was at Texas A&M in College Station, and then Thursday he was back in H-Town at the University of Houston to register college students to vote.
Beto and Powered by People are prioritizing the young people who all too often written off by the political establishment.
In a state as big as Texas, it’s going to take this kind of work ethic to meet the voters who can help us win.
Our program – registering and confirming voter registrations for young people and then personally staying in touch with them for the duration of the election cycle – produces results. In 2024, voters in our program voted at a rate of 79%. Otherwise, young people in Texas turned out at a meager 37%. This is the work that works.
We have a historic opportunity this November to elect James Talarico, secure the 51st Democratic seat in the Senate, and help Democrats win up and down the ballot. To get there, our goal is to mobilize 100,000 voters ahead of the midterms.

clean_body: On Monday, Beto flew from El Paso to Houston to work with Powered by People volunteers at Texas Southern University. Afterwards he drove to Austin that night to meet volunteers the next morning at the University of Texas at Austin. The next day he was at Texas A&M in College Station, and then Thursday he was back in H-Town at the University of Houston to register college students to vote. Beto and Powered by People are prioritizing the young people who all too often written off by the political establishment. In a state as big as Texas, it’s going to take this kind of work ethic to meet the voters who can help us win. Our program – registering and confirming voter registrations for young people and then personally staying in touch with them for the duration of the election cycle – produces results. In 2024, voters in our program voted at a rate of 79%. Otherwise, young people in Texas turned out at a meager 37%. This is the work that works. We have a historic opportunity this November to elect James Talarico, secure the 51st Democratic seat in the Senate, and help Democrats win up and down the ballot. To get there, our goal is to mobilize 100,000 voters ahead of the midterms. Thank you, Team Powered by People

We’re excited to announce UAW President Shawn Fain is our Keynote Speaker for our 2026 Indiana Democratic Party Salute to Labor! We’d love to see you there – = Born and raised in Kokomo, Shawn Fain has taken the Hoosier spirit to the fight for high wages, good benefits, and safe working conditions for every single American worker. This will be an exciting event featuring President Fain, Chair Karen Tallian, and Hoosier Democrats who fight for you every single day. You won’t want to miss President Fain’s return to Indiana – = AES-BlackRock Deal: Democrats Proposed State Oversight for Sale of Public Utilities to Private Equity. Republicans Voted It Down. This week, Hoosiers learned that private equity firm BlackRock is purchasing AES utilities. was being bought out by a $33 billion consortium led by private equity firm BlackRock. This $33 billion buyout will lead to higher prices and worse services for Hoosiers as BlackRock seeks to maximize profits. During the legislative session, Democrats proposed a to address immediate utility affordability and require state oversight before a public utility could be sold to private investors. Republicans sold Hoosiers out once again and voted down every single one of these amendments. 20+ years of Republican control in Indiana has created an affordability crisis that gets worse every day. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. On Thursday, the U.S. House voted on a War Powers Resolution to curb the Trump administration’s war in Iran. Every single Indiana Republican voted NO, blocking transparency, accountability, and a debate that the American people deserve before our service members are sent to war. Hoosier Democratic Reps. Frank Mrvan and André Carson vote YES to demand Congressional oversight. In the Senate, it was largely the same. Republicans, including Sens. Young and Banks from Indiana, voted to block any Congressional action on Trump’s war. name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: The biggest swing at TABOR yet
body:
I’m running for State Treasurer because Trump and TABOR are crushing Colorado. I’m already fighting back.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9728aed98a07/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10373962?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=533deec357&e=b48bb2b4f4)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
I’m running for State Treasurer because Trump and TABOR are crushing Colorado.
I’m already fighting back.
**Yesterday I introduced a bill in partnership with Colorado teachers to raise our TABOR cap to invest more in K-12 public education. It’s a huge swing at TABOR—the biggest change since it was created in 1992.**
The fiscal rules we operate under as a state haven’t kept up with reality. Colorado is trying to run a 21st-century education system under rules written in 1992.
[**Colorado Public Radio just reported on this breaking news. Learn more here.**](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=8a214bbdfe&e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=3397491be6&e=b48bb2b4f4)
| |
Our teachers are doing heroic work. Our students are producing incredible results. But Colorado ranks near the bottom nationally in what we invest in K–12 education, and we have one of the largest teacher pay penalties in the country.
This measure asks Coloradans whether we want to keep funding our schools near the bottom of the country... or whether we want to lead.
**Nothing radical. Nothing reckless. Just the simple idea that when Colorado’s economy grows, our investment in education should grow with it.**
**If you’re looking for a State Treasurer willing to stand up to the financial constraints holding Colorado back, I don’t just talk about it—I’m doing it.**

I think our schools should be as strong as Colorado. If you agree, I’d be honored to have your support. Call or text your thoughts on TABOR to my personal cell, 303-358-5551. No swear words please! 😂
---
| | Talk soon,
P.S. It’s been awesome seeing such incredible turnout at caucuses across the state. If you see me at your caucus or assembly, come say hi and get a button!
---

After a client secured an arbitration award in a property development dispute, the Texas-based partner needed a judge to enforce it. For the first time, he considered the state's nascent business court as an alternative to the traditional district court system.

"Let's go see if we have jurisdiction," Napoli said he thought before filing in November.

The addition of arbitration agreement enforcement is one of several expansions to the Texas Business Court's jurisdiction that went into effect Sept. 1, sparking an uptick in activity from corporate litigators. **" Cornyn goes on offense against Paxton as Republicans await Trump's endorsement"** AP's **Tom Beaumont** - As Texas waits on President**Donald Trump 's **[promised endorsement](https://substack.com/redirect/f145b65d-bb25-4df4-b415-70da3153f71e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Sen. **John Cornyn** isn't holding back on his runoff opponent in the Republican primary.

His campaign is releasing a [new video](https://substack.com/redirect/ca61f3d4-77c8-49c0-b951-4da531b25732?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday with a litany of ethical and personal accusations against state Attorney General **Ken Paxton**. It's an initial salvo in a second round of campaigning that could be even more bitter and expensive than the first.

The video revisits issues like Paxton's impeachment trial on corruption charges, which ended in an acquittal but exposed an extramarital affair, and a state fraud indictment for securities fraud, which Paxton resolved with a plea deal without admitting guilt.

Cornyn's team said it's spending tens of thousands of dollars to keep the video in front of voters' eyes. It's pocket change in a race where spending surpassed $110 million before Tuesday, but a possible foreshadowing of a future deluge if the six-minute clip is edited into television spots.

Trump did not endorse a candidate in the primary, frustrating Republicans who fear that they're wasting time and resources in Texas that could be devoted to more competitive battleground states. The president said Wednesday that he would weigh in on the May 26 runoff and expect the candidate without his endorsement to drop out, but he hasn't announced a decision.

Cornyn narrowly finished first in the primary that ended on Tuesday, but he did not cross the 50%-plus threshold necessary to avoid a runoff. U.S. Rep. **Wesley Hunt** finished third and was disqualified.

Party leaders are pushing for Cornyn, a stalwart incumbent seeking his fifth term, and warn that Paxton has too much baggage to be successful in a November general election against **James Talarico** , the Democratic nominee.

But Paxton has proven resilient to attacks over the years, and he's fashioned himself as a political warrior for Trump's "Make America Great Again" movement. He told conservative influencer Benny Johnson that he wouldn't drop out, no matter what happens with the endorsement.

"I'm going to give people in Texas a choice," Paxton said. "The people in Washington can have their own opinion. The president can have his own opinion."

Paxton made a different offer on social media. There, he said he would consider dropping out if Senate Republican leaders lifted the filibuster to pass legislation supported by Trump to create strict new proof-of-citizenship requirements for voting. The proposal has [stalled in the Senate.](https://substack.com/redirect/0d894ffe-104b-4801-9d4a-214802f149b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Trump appeared frustrated by Paxton's intransigence.

"That is bad for him," he told Politico. "So maybe, maybe that leads me to go the other direction."

The president previously wrote on social media that he would endorse a Texas candidate because the divisive contest cannot "be allowed to go on any longer."

**" Dallas City Council backs dual track on City Hall, repairs and possible move"** [Dallas News's](https://substack.com/redirect/e95f7871-48ea-4a9f-aae9-30dd62afa3d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **None** - A deeply divided Dallas City Council is hedging its bets on City Hall, exploring relocation while also ordering plans to repair the aging building.

After hours of scrutiny, debate and amendments, the council voted 9-6 to approve a compromise resolution that forces the city to pursue those two tracks and bars consultants that recently assessed the building's conditions bidding on contracts related to the project.

The action came just after 1 a.m. Thursday, a major step in deciding the fate of the nearly 50-year-old City Hall and the prime downtown site developers covet but preservationists want to keep.

The nine council members who supported it said Dallas needs more concrete information before deciding whether to repair the aging building or abandon it.

The backers were Mayor **Eric Johnson** and council members **Gay Donnell Willis** , **Chad West** , **Jesse Moreno** , **Zarin Gracey** , **Maxie Johnson** , **Jaime Resendez** , **Lorie Blair** and **Kathy Stewart**.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/efaa6f41-f999-459c-90a0-49158fcbfe36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" In hopes of thwarting ICE, San Antonio moves to place moratorium on private detention centers"** [San Antonio Report's](https://substack.com/redirect/a5100a12-b2dd-4547-a367-1e93c54baae8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Diego Medel** - San Antonio City Council on Thursday directed city staff to explore zoning and development code changes governing detention facilities while initiating a moratorium on any new private detention centers.

The action followed a City Manager's report updating council on a February resolution that asked staff to evaluate what actions San Antonio could legally take in response to immigration enforcement activity and a newly purchased ICE detention facility expected to operate on the East Side.

The new resolution directs staff to examine potential changes to the city's Unified Development Code, the city's primary land-use planning ordinance, that could establish detention facilities as a defined land use and require City Council approval before such facilities could be developed in the future.

Council also approved an amendment introduced by District 2 Councilman **Jalen McKee-Rodriguez** instructing city staff to begin the process of creating a moratorium -- a temporary halt on new development approvals -- for private detention facilities.

(_[SA REPORT](https://substack.com/redirect/bbdd6527-7159-4ba4-87eb-2972ffb0c513?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" ICE moving toward closing El Paso detention camp, report says"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/2607f786-03fc-4ef6-bff6-3eb1eb89609c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Ayden Runnels, Lomi Kriel** - Camp East Montana, a hastily constructed immigration detention facility in El Paso currently experiencing a measles outbreak, is in the process of being closed by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, according to a report from the Washington Post.

A document was distributed to ICE staff, the Post reports, indicating the agency was drafting a letter to terminate the facility's $1.2 billion contract at an unspecified date. The facility's contract with Acquisition Logistics LLC is set to expire on Sept. 30, 2027. A spokesperson with the company did not respond to an immediate request for comment.

News of the potential closure of the facility located on the Fort Bliss U.S. Army base prompted immediate response from U.S. Rep. **Veronica Escobar** , D-El Paso, who called the camp the "epitome of fraud, waste, [and] abuse." Escobar has led calls to close the facility.

* **BUSINESS NEWS**

**" $100 a barrel? How the war in Iran could affect oil and gas prices in Houston"** [Houston Chronicle's](https://substack.com/redirect/710ebdf6-b4ab-41a8-bab0-ff83bb68f294?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Amanda Drane** - Oil prices could surge to $100 a barrel if war with Iran continues, delivering a boost for Houston's oil industry and pain at the pump for American consumers.

The conflict is choking off oil and gas tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical artery for 15% of the world's oil supply and 20% of natural gas cargoes. Oil prices surged 13% since Thursday, leveling out around $71 in Monday afternoon trading.

Just how much the price of oil could jump and how much impact Houston will feel depends on how long the conflict hampers global oil trade.

"If the reduction in tanker traffic continues for a week or so, it will be historic," **Jim Burkhard** , S&P Global's vice president and global head of crude oil research, said in a statement. "Beyond that it would be epochal for the oil market with prices rising to ration scarce supply and impacts in financial markets."

Here's what to know about how Houston could be affected by the conflict that threatens to spark the biggest oil supply disruption in history.

**" Texas court weighs beach access limits due to SpaceX launches"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/71190ccb-9f8c-45e6-aaa9-c0c38a5ddbed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Berenice Garcia** - The Texas Supreme Court pondered how far the state can go in limiting access to a public beach during oral arguments Thursday in a case involving the closure of Boca Chica Beach for SpaceX's rocket launches.

Rio Grande Valley environmentalist and indigenous groups are suing the Texas General Land Office and Cameron County over a law, passed in 2013, that allows some counties to temporarily close a beach for space flight activities.

The lawsuit is among multiple waged over the years between local advocates and SpaceX as the space exploration company has continued to expand its physical footprint and the frequency of its rocket launches in South Texas. Both, activists argue, have caused harm to the local environment and impeded the public's ability to access a beach that has to be closed off for safety when SpaceX is conducting its test launches.

Apple is doubling its Houston manufacturing footprint and preparing to launch a new training facility in an expansion that could create thousands of jobs.

The tech giant announced Tuesday it will produce Mac minis in the United States for the first time at its Houston campus. The iPhone maker also will expand its existing AI server manufacturing operations here, bringing its total local footprint to 500,000 square feet.

To support its U.S. expansion plans, Apple is building a 20,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing training center in Houston that is expected to open later this year. The center, already under construction at Apple's north Houston campus, "will provide hands-on training in advanced manufacturing techniques to students, supplier employees and American businesses of all sizes," the company said in a news release.

The Houston facility will operate under a model similar to Apple's training center that opened in Detroit in 2025. There, small- and medium-sized businesses can enroll in free classes on integrating artificial intelligence into their operations.

TOP NEWS " DA Jose Garza closes review of officers who stopped Austin shooter" Tony Plohetski - A memorial to the victims of a mass shooting at Buford's bar on West 6th Street on Monday March 2, 2026, a day after a mass shooting. Travis County District Attorney Jos e Garza on Wednesday clarified that he plans to take no action against the three Austin police officers who opened fire early Sunday on a mass shooter who killed three people and injured 13 others on a bar-lined stretch of West Sixth Street. Ndiaga Diagne , the suspected gunman, was mid-rampage when the officers fatally shot him. In a one-page letter to Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis , Garza said his office's Civil Rights Unit conducted a "thorough review of the evidence," including video, a walk-through of the scene and coordination with the Austin Police Department's Special Investigations Unit. "After the review, it is clear and indisputable that at the time the officers were responding to an active shooting in a mass casualty situation, and that the subject of the shooting was in the act of using unlawful deadly force," Garza wrote. () " Camp Mystic ordered not to alter flood-damaged areas amid suit" Emily Foxhall - Camp Mystic cannot alter its property by the Guadalupe River where 27 girls and the camp's executive director died last summer, so that evidence can be preserved while a lawsuit proceeds, a judge in Austin ruled Wednesday. The camp cannot demolish, repair or reconstruct a number of cabins where campers slept when a massive flood struck on July 4, Travis County District Court Judge Maya Guerra Gamble said. The camp also cannot modify its grounds or its office building, recreation hall or commissary -- all points of interest in the wrongful death case filed by the parents of camper Cile Steward , whose body still has not been found. But the court order, which will be finalized in the coming days, doesn't block Camp Mystic from reopening its neighboring (camp). () " Texas Business Court Attracts More Cases Under Lower Entry Bar" via - Akerman LLC's Michael Napoli had a choice to make. After a client secured an arbitration award in a property development dispute, the Texas-based partner needed a judge to enforce it. For the first time, he considered the state's nascent business court as an alternative to the traditional district court system. "Let's go see if we have jurisdiction," Napoli said he thought before filing in November. The addition of arbitration agreement enforcement is one of several expansions to the Texas Business Court's jurisdiction that went into effect Sept. 1, sparking an uptick in activity from corporate litigators. The court drew 141 new filings from September through February, a 76% year-over-year increase from the 80 cases filed in court's first six months of operations. On average, the number of weekly filings has increased to five in year two from three in year one. () 2026 " Trump calls for Texas GOP Senate primary to end, vows endorsement soon of Cornyn or Paxton" via - President Donald Trump on Wednesday demanded an end to the Republican Senate race in Texas, promising to soon endorse either incumbent Sen. John Cornyn or his challenger Attorney General Ken Paxton. The candidate who does not receive his backing should immediately quit the race, the president said. Meanwhile, Democrats quickly rallied behind their nominee, state Rep. James Talarico of Austin. The GOP race, however, is far from settled. After being locked in a bitter primary for many months, Cornyn and Paxton now face a May 26 runoff that promises to become an even more expensive and caustic campaign - which Trump said should not happen. The faceoff must end for the good of the party and the country, Trump posted on Truth Social. "I will be making my Endorsement soon, and will be asking the candidate that I don't Endorse to immediately DROP OUT OF THE RACE!" Trump said. "Is that fair? We must win in November!!!" () " Cornyn goes on offense against Paxton as Republicans await Trump's endorsement" AP's Tom Beaumont - As Texas waits on PresidentDonald Trump 's , Sen. John Cornyn isn't holding back on his runoff opponent in the Republican primary. His campaign is releasing a Thursday with a litany of ethical and personal accusations against state Attorney General Ken Paxton. It's an initial salvo in a second round of campaigning that could be even more bitter and expensive than the first. The video revisits issues like Paxton's impeachment trial on corruption charges, which ended in an acquittal but exposed an extramarital affair, and a state fraud indictment for securities fraud, which Paxton resolved with a plea deal without admitting guilt. Cornyn's team said it's spending tens of thousands of dollars to keep the video in front of voters' eyes. It's pocket change in a race where spending surpassed $110 million before Tuesday, but a possible foreshadowing of a future deluge if the six-minute clip is edited into television spots. Trump did not endorse a candidate in the primary, frustrating Republicans who fear that they're wasting time and resources in Texas that could be devoted to more competitive battleground states. The president said Wednesday that he would weigh in on the May 26 runoff and expect the candidate without his endorsement to drop out, but he hasn't announced a decision. Cornyn narrowly finished first in the primary that ended on Tuesday, but he did not cross the 50%-plus threshold necessary to avoid a runoff. U.S. Rep. Wesley Hunt finished third and was disqualified. Party leaders are pushing for Cornyn, a stalwart incumbent seeking his fifth term, and warn that Paxton has too much baggage to be successful in a November general election against James Talarico , the Democratic nominee. But Paxton has proven resilient to attacks over the years, and he's fashioned himself as a political warrior for Trump's "Make America Great Again" movement. He told conservative influencer Benny Johnson that he wouldn't drop out, no matter what happens with the endorsement. "I'm going to give people in Texas a choice," Paxton said. "The people in Washington can have their own opinion. The president can have his own opinion." Paxton made a different offer on social media. There, he said he would consider dropping out if Senate Republican leaders lifted the filibuster to pass legislation supported by Trump to create strict new proof-of-citizenship requirements for voting. The proposal has Trump appeared frustrated by Paxton's intransigence. "That is bad for him," he told Politico. "So maybe, maybe that leads me to go the other direction." The president previously wrote on social media that he would endorse a Texas candidate because the divisive contest cannot "be allowed to go on any longer." Gonzales admitted to the affair earlier this week, and faced pressure from top Republican leaders who urged him to withdraw his candidacy while the U.S. House Ethics Committee looks into the matter. David Lowe , Terri Leo-Wilson , Mark Dorazio and Andy Hopper , all gambling opponents, defeated primary challenges from candidates backed by billionaire Miriam Adelson 's Las Vegas Sands casino empire on Tuesday. Outspoken anti-gambling activist Cheryl Bean also overcame opposition from Texas Sands PAC and Texas Defense PAC -- super PACs funded by the casino company -- in the open race for the Republican nomination to represent House District 94 in Tarrant County. John Creuzot , the top prosecutor in Dallas County since 2019, trailed the former judge Givens into the overnight hours before announcing shortly before noon Wednesday that he had conceded the race. "I want to first express my deepest gratitude to my family, supporters, and every voter who placed their trust in me throughout this campaign," Creuzot said in a statement. "While the outcome was not what we had hoped for, I am proud of the work my team accomplished and the important conversations we advanced about justice, accountability, and public safety in Dallas County." Amber Givens had earned nearly 54% of the vote to Creuzot's 46.15% in Tuesday's election. There were no Republicans running in the primary election, paving the way for Givens to take office after the November general election. As of 8:27 p.m., with early voting totals reported, Nirenberg had 62% of the vote compared with Sakai's 38%, according to results from the Bexar County Elections Department. The result unseats a first-term incumbent in one of the most powerful elected positions in local government. The Bexar County judge is the county's top elected official and presides over the Commissioners Court, which oversees county government. Nirenberg, who has never lost an election, will face Republican nominee Patrick Von Dohlen this fall. Von Dohlen ran unopposed for the nomination. Wong collected 23,825 votes to claim the Republican nomination outright, avoiding a runoff. Kenneth Omoruyi finished second with about 13%, followed by Daryl Aaron at nearly 12% and Melissa M. Wilson at just over 11%. George, the incumbent, came in last with 3,478 votes out of 42,568 cast. On the Democratic side, Dexter L. Christian Becerra came in third at about 17%, followed by Cynthia Lenton-Gary at 15% and Eddie Sajjad at 7%. () " Six San Antonio-area judges fall in Democratic primary upsets" Andrea Drusch - In an election night filled with dramatic upsets and unexpected results, six San Antonio-area incumbent judges fell to Democratic primary challengers. Judicial races typically don't get much attention on a crowded ballot with higher-profile races, and many voters who typically don't vote in primaries were drawn out this year in frustration with President Donald Trump. Among the judges who were swept out were William "Cruz" Shaw, a popular former City Council member who lost his primary reelection to a juvenile district court in Bexar County, falling to Raymond A. Villareal , a former staffer in the Attorney General's office who recently wrote a vampire novel and took 52% of the vote in Tuesday's Democratic primary. "I have no clue what happened. I didn't see my opponent at all during the campaign trail. He doesn't practice juvenile law," Shaw said Wednesday. "It's crazy. It doesn't matter how hard you work, how much money you raise, how good of a job you do. It does not matter. Most people don't step into a courtroom, they don't see what we do on a daily basis, so they just vote based off name," he said. Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath in a statement Wednesday said the Texas Education Agency "will move forward with the selection of a new superintendent" to replace Karen Molinar , who was named superintendent in March 2025. However, it was announced in October that the struggling district would be taken over by the Texas Education Agency, an intervention required by state law due to one of the district's campuses receiving a fifth straight unacceptable academic accountability rating. The state takeover includes appointing a new board of managers for the school district, and now, apparently, a new superintendent. Other popular cryptos, including Ethereum, have also been plunging, and some analysts have been warning much steeper drops could be coming. Early Monday, Bitcoin posted something of a rebound, pushing back near $70,000, although the digital coin was still off more than 20% year-to-date.
